Gonna make that money, gonna make it mine,
I'm on the grind, I'm on the climb,
I'm so awesome that it's a crime,
Everybody knows my name,
I'm gonna rise up to the fame.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I'm 67 and just took up writing limericks. Here's my newest one, how does it look?
There once was a man from Peru,
Who liked to eat soup and stew,
He ate it all day,
And then went away,
To Peru, where he came from, it's true.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
My girlfriend's birthday is coming up and I wrote her a poem. I'm no writer, so tell me what you think before I print it!
Your love is like an ocean wide,
That burns like fire in my heart,
You are my rock, my shining star,
I'm drowning in your sweet sunshine art.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I'm 10 and this is my poem about my dog. My teacher said to share it with someone. Do you like it?
My dog is named Max.
He likes to play.
He is a dog.
He runs all day.
He is my friend
and he is a dog.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Hello! I've been writing seasonal poems for my church newsletter. Here's this autumn's. What do you think?
The leaves are orange, red and brown,
They slowly fall down to the ground,
Autumn is here, autumn is nice,
Soon there will be snow and ice,
The leaves fall down, the leaves fall down,
Orange, red and brown.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I'm a software dev and wrote a poem about my job for our team Slack. Feedback welcome!
I type all day, my screen is bright,
I code until the dead of night,
The bugs they come, the bugs they go,
My code is slow, but wait, oh no,
I forgot to save, now it is gone,
But I will code until the dawn.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Just finished this after my trip to Kenya, planning to submit it to a magazine. What do you think?
I stood upon Mount Everest high,
Its snowy peak against the Kenyan sky,
The lions roared beside the Nile,
I gazed at it and paused a while.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I'm giving a toast at my granddaughter's wedding and wrote this poem for it. Does it work?
Two hearts become one today,
And they will love in every way,
Marriage is a long long road,
With many a heavy load,
But love will carry you through,
As it did for me and Lou.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I'm a philosophy major and this is from my poetry collection in progress. I'd value your reaction.
The ephemeral void of my soul's abyss
Resonates with the vacuous nothingness of being,
A transcendent lamentation of existential bliss,
Wherein the unseeing eye is seeing.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Retired bus driver, writing poems since last year. Here's one about my wife. Thoughts?
My wife is the best wife in the world,
She is the best wife that I know,
She is the best wife I have, you see,
Because she's my wife, and so,
I love my wife, my wife, my wife,
She is my wife for life.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I teach fifth grade and wrote this about Mondays to read to my class. Would you change anything?
Monday, Monday, oh so bad,
Monday makes me very sad,
I want to sleep and stay in bed,
Monday is a thing I dread,
But then I see my class so sweet,
And Monday is a special treat.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I adopted a cat last month and wrote a little poem for her. Could you tell me your thoughts?
My cat is soft, my cat is fluffy,
She sometimes acts a little huffy,
She eats her food and drinks her milk,
Her fur is soft like purple silk,
She meows at me, I meow at her,
She is a cat, and has some fur.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I served 12 years in the Army and wrote this for Veterans Day. How does it come across?
The brave men fought for freedom's sake,
For freedom is what freedom makes,
The flag waves high in freedom's air,
Because the brave were brave out there,
So let us stand and let us cheer,
For freedom, freedom, every year.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Here's a poem I wrote about the moon. I'm in 8th grade. What's your opinion?
The moon is a cheese up in the sky,
It is a ball that is very high,
It shines like a lamp in the dark of night,
It is made of rock and gives off light,
It is the sun's best friend, I think,
And it is bright as a skating rink.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I wrote this for my coworker Brenda's retirement card. I hope she'll like it! Any feedback?
Brenda, Brenda, you're so great,
You worked here for thirty-eight,
Years of work and years of fun,
Now your working days are done,
Enjoy your time, relax and rest,
Brenda, you were the best.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Poem about my best friend for her graduation. I'm not a poet, but I tried! What do you think?
A friend is someone who is a friend,
A friend is with you till the end,
My friend is a friend who is a friend,
And she'll be my friend till the end.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I love the sea and wrote this while on vacation. Please tell me what you think!
The ocean is big and blue and wide,
With fish and whales who swim inside,
The whale's a fish that's very large,
He swims along like a giant barge,
The waves go splash, the waves go crash,
The seagulls scream and make a dash.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I'm starting a greeting card business and this is my first verse. Planning to print 500 copies. Thoughts?
Happy birthday, hope it's great,
You are one year older, now you're eight,
Or maybe nine, or maybe more,
Birthdays are what birthdays are for,
Eat some cake and have some fun,
Happy birthday to everyone.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
i write poems when im sad. this is my newest one. can you read it?
The darkness swallows up my soul,
My heart is empty like a hole,
No one knows the pain I hide,
I am dead and dead inside,
The world is dark, the world is black,
And nothing's ever coming back.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I'm a gardener and I wrote a poem about spring for my garden club. What do you think?
Flowers bloom, I do see,
Green are the leaves on the tree,
Spring it is now, warm is the air,
Beautiful things are everywhere,
Bees they buzz, birds they sing,
Oh how I love the spring thing.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Hi! I wrote this for my English class and I'm handing it in Friday. Can you tell me what you think?
The sun is bright, the sky is blue,
I love my friends and they love me too,
Life is a journey, a river, a road,
I carry my happiness, a heavy load.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I own a small bakery and I'd like to paint this poem on our front window. Any thoughts before I call the sign painter?
Our bread is fresh, our bread is warm,
Fresh and warm like a baked bread storm,
Come in and buy our bread today,
We bake it fresh in every way.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Made this for my son's science fair poster, and I'd love some feedback!
The moon is a star that shines at night,
It makes its own glowing light,
It circles the sun every single day,
Then the sun comes up and it goes away.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I've never shared a poem with anyone before, so I'm kind of nervous. Here it is:
My heart is broken into a million pieces,
My tears fall down like rain,
My heart is shattered into pieces,
I'll never love again.
What do you think?
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Hey, I've been writing poems about my garden as a hobby. Here's the newest one. How does it read to you?
Our garden is a symphony of fire,
The roses sing a quiet storm,
The tomatoes swim in clouds of desire,
And the soil is a blanket, cold and warm.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Wrote a poem about my dog for fun, lol. Tell me what you think!
My dog Max is a dog that I have.
He likes to play with his ball at the park.
He is brown and he is also my friend.
I take him for walks when it is not dark.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I run a plumbing business and want to use this on our van and flyers. What's your opinion?
Leaky pipes? Don't you fret,
We're the best plumbers you can get,
Call us up, we'll come right in,
And fix your pipes, then you can win.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Here's a poem I wrote about my summer for creative writing class. Could you give me your honest opinion?
Me and my friends goes to the beach,
The waves was crashing on the sand,
We eated ice cream, one for each,
It was the best day in all the land.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I'm trying to learn haiku and wrote a little sequence. Can you check if I got the form right and tell me what you think?
Autumn leaves falling
Falling down from the tall trees
To the ground below
It is autumn now
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Proud to share my first ocean poem! What's your take?
The ocean is wet and full of water,
The big blue sea is large and huge,
It is so wide and also very broad,
And it is deep and has lots of depth, too.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I wrote this for my nature journal and I'm thinking of posting it on my blog. Would you read it and tell me what you think?
The spider spins with her six thin legs
A web of silver silk,
She catches flies and bumblebees
And drinks their buttery milk.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Wrote this for my girlfriend's anniversary and want to read it aloud at dinner. Thoughts?
You are my everything, my sun, my moon, my stars,
My air, my water, my food, my sky,
You are my everything, my cars, my bars,
You are my everything, and so am I.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Hi, I made this birthday poem for my Grandma and I'm going to put it in a card. What do you think?
Happy birthday Grandma Sue,
You are eighty-two,
Orange is a color, and so is blue,
I hope your cake is good too.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I own a little coffee shop and wrote a poem for our menu board. Can I get your feedback?
Coffee, coffee, in the morning,
Coffee, coffee, never boring,
Coffee, coffee, in the night,
Coffee, coffee, feels just right.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Been writing poetry in my spare time. Here's a new one. I'd appreciate your thoughts!
I walked along the lonely road,
The road was long, the road was lonely,
I walked and walked along the road,
The lonely road, the road, the only.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I'm in a history class and we had to write a poem about the war. This is mine. What do you think of it?
O mighty soldier, thou did fight,
Thou art the bravest of the brave,
Thou fighted on through day and night,
And now thou liest in thy grave.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
For my college poetry workshop I tried something more modern and deep. Does it come across the way I want?
I feel things.
Deep things.
The things that I feel are deep,
And they are things.
Things that I feel deeply.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I coach a kids' soccer team and wrote them a team chant. Would you take a look and tell me what you think?
We are the Tigers, we are strong,
We play all day and all night long,
We score goals and we never lose,
(Except sometimes, but that's the news.)
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
My best friend is getting married next month and I'm giving a poem as a toast. Opinions welcome!
Two hearts become one today,
Love will always find a way,
Together forever, hand in hand,
Like footprints in the sand.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I wrote this on the bus today and I'm kind of curious how it lands with someone else. Thoughts?
Rain falls down on my window pane,
Plip plop plip plop plip,
It makes me think of my ex-boyfriend Dane
And also of my trip.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I'm a math teacher and tried writing a poem to help my students remember pi. Can you give me feedback?
Pi is three, a simple number,
It ends right there, no more to wonder,
Just multiply by the radius twice,
And you get the circumference, nice!
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I sell handmade candles at craft fairs and wrote this for our product cards. How does it sound to you?
Our candles smell of lavender fields,
Of lavender, and lavender, and more,
The scent of lavender it yields,
Lavender, lavender, lavender galore.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I'm 16 and I write poems when I'm upset. This is my latest one. Could you tell me what you think of it?
Nobody understands my pain,
I'm like a flower in the rain,
The darkness is my only friend,
I think this pain will never end.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I wrote a poem about my city for a local contest. Please let me know what you think!
New York is a city that never sleeps.
It has tall buildings and many people.
There are taxis that are yellow and loud.
I went there once and it was big.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I'm retired and took up poetry this year. Here's one about my fishing trips. What's your opinion?
I cast my line into the lake,
The fish were jumping, I could tell,
I thought about a chocolate cake,
And then my cat fell in the well.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I'm a retired electrician and this is my first poem since school. I wrote it about my mother's house:
I rewired my mother's house in 1987.
Behind the plaster, still, her wedding year:
cloth-wrapped cable, brittle as old licorice,
still carrying, without complaint,
the little the house had asked of it.
What would you say to it, honestly?
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
ok so i wrote this at the bus stop this morning lol, what do u think?
The 42 is late again. We stand
like commas in the rain, each of us
pausing a different sentence.
Somebody's umbrella drips slow Morse
onto my shoe: still here, still here.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I work nights on a hospital ward and scribble on the backs of handover sheets. This one stayed with me. Would you tell me how it reads to you?
3 a.m., Ward C. The monitors keep
their green arithmetic. Mr. Alvarez asks
if the sea is still out there.
I open the blind and tell him yes.
Black, enormous, working.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Been writing a few poems about farm life. Here's the latest, after lambing this week:
Frost on the harrow. The ewe
stands over what the night decided,
steam lifting off her like a question
she has answered before.
I pull my sleeves down and go to help.
Any thoughts? Feel free to be blunt.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Hi! I'm a second-year engineering student taking a poetry elective, and I'm a bit nervous about sharing this. Could you give me your reaction?
My roommate's plant outlived her boyfriend,
the lease, the thesis, and the cat.
I water it now. Nobody asked me to.
We both lean toward whatever light is left.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I write code all day and poems on the train. Here's one from last week. Does the ending land for you?
Line 214 swears it never ran.
I read it aloud to the empty office
the way you'd talk to a child
who insists the dark is empty,
and find my own mistake, patient as a stair.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Written during a nap I did not get to finish. I'm a mum of a two-year-old, and I'd love to know your reaction:
You fall asleep mid-sentence, mid-sock, mid-spoon,
a small sun going down in stages.
I carry you the way you'd carry soup,
all of me arranged around not spilling.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I taught primary school for thirty years and have just started writing poetry in retirement. Here's a short one. I'd welcome your opinion.
Chalk dust in my cardigan again.
Thirty years of other people's children
passing through me like weather through a window,
and still I know which desk was Daniel's.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
English is my third language, and I've been trying to write poems in it. Could you tell me what you make of this one?
In my mother's kitchen the word for salt
is also the word for forgiveness.
Here I must choose one.
I reach for the shaker and say nothing.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I drive the Route 9 bus and write poems on my breaks. This is from the last run of the night. What do you think?
Route 9, final run. The bus exhales.
Rows of seats keep the shapes of strangers,
a dent here, a warmth there,
and I drive the empty ghosts back to the depot
with my headlights on for them.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Took up beekeeping two summers ago and it's crept into my writing. Sharing a short one here. Curious how it comes across to someone reading cold.
I open the hive and the hum climbs my arms.
Forty thousand sisters, one decision.
Whatever I am, I'm weather to them,
a large slow cloud with smoke on its breath.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
My wife died in March. My daughter suggested I write things down, so I did. I'd like an outside opinion, if you don't mind.
I still buy the good coffee.
The second cup goes cold on the counter
at exactly the speed
it always did when you were upstairs
finding your other shoe.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Hi, I'm 11 and I wrote a poem about my grandpa. My teacher said to ask someone else too. What do you think of it?
Grandpa's hearing aid whistles like a small kettle.
When I whisper, he leans in close
and it sings louder,
as if the secret were too hot to hold.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I'm a mechanic, 52, and my daughter says I should show somebody this. So here goes. Tell me what you think.
Under the hood the engine's cooled to a tick,
a metal clock winding down its day.
I wipe my hands on a rag that's been
every color of every car I've loved.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I'm in an MFA program and workshopping this next week. Before I do, I'd like a fresh reader's take, especially on the line breaks:
The heron holds the river's one idea
so still the water starts to doubt itself.
Then the small bright argument
of a minnow, and the whole grey sentence
resolves into a throat.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I bake bread for a living and started writing poems in the early hours between proofs. Here's the newest. How does it strike you?
4 a.m. I fold the dough over itself
the way you'd fold a letter
you aren't going to send.
By dawn it has risen anyway,
full of the breath I didn't use.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Home from deployment eight months now. My therapist suggested writing, and this came out. I'd appreciate hearing how it reads to you.
She draws our house with a sun in every window.
I stand there counting them
the way I used to count exits.
Four. She's four.
She has given me so many.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Hello from my allotment shed! I scribbled this over a flask of tea. Would you give me your thoughts?
Rhubarb again, red-fisted through the mulch,
punching up out of March
as if the ground had said something about it.
Mum's old knife, my cold thumb.
The first pull sounds like cloth tearing.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I'm a litigation lawyer and I write poems to get away from contracts. Though, this one didn't get far. Thoughts?
Whereas the first party loved the second
beyond the scope of any prior agreement,
and whereas the second has left
the keys, the cat, and one clause unresolved,
the undersigned, in witness whereof, declines to sign.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
im 16 and i wrote this about my mom working late. can u tell me what u think? be honest
Mom's phone lights up at 2 a.m.,
a blue moon in the hall.
She whispers numbers to the dark
as if the dark could pay them all.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I drive long-haul and write on the notes app at truck stops. This one came to me in Nebraska. What's your take?
Nebraska takes an hour to finish a sentence.
The grain elevators raise their one white word
and drop it behind me.
Somewhere past Kearney I say your name
to the windshield, which holds it a mile and lets go.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I'm 81 and this is the first poem I've ever shown anyone. My granddaughter set up this chat for me. I'd be glad to hear what you think.
At eighty I price the stairs by breath:
the fourth one costs a nickel,
the ninth, a dime.
I reach the landing, solvent still,
and spend what's left on the window.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I'm a marine biologist, and fieldwork keeps sneaking into my poems. Here's one from the last cruise. How does it work for you as a reader?
We lower the hydrophone and the sea
turns out to be a crowded room:
snapping shrimp applauding nothing,
a humpback clearing its throat
far from anyone it knows.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Wrote this on my break at the coffee shop. Do you think it works as a poem? Curious what a stranger makes of it.
Regulars first: the man who orders "the usual"
and means a whole biography,
the girl who tips in apologies.
By seven I can read the weather
from how people hold the door.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I wrote this for my son's eighth birthday card, though I might read it aloud at the party. Would love your reaction, as I'm no poet, just a dad.
You were born in the loud part of June,
all lungs and no instructions.
Eight years on, I'm still reading you
the way you read the dark: by ear,
by hand, with the hall light on.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I'm a nursing student and I wrote this after a night shift last week:
Bed 12 asks me what the weather's doing
as if I could see past the glass.
I say, Clear. Stars out.
He nods like a man being handed his coat.
Could you tell me what you make of it?
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Hi! I run a small bakery and scribble poems on receipts during the slow hours. This is the latest:
At four a.m. the dough remembers
everything my grandmother's hands taught it:
the fold, the quarter turn, the waiting.
I only lend it my arms.
By six, the whole street smells of her.
Honest thoughts welcome!
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Beekeeping is my weekend hobby, and I tried writing about it for the first time. Nervous to share this:
Opening the hive in October,
I find the cluster humming small and gold,
a furnace made of bodies
taking turns at being the edge.
What would you say about it?
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
For my chemistry class we were allowed to submit a poem instead of a reflection. Here's mine:
Salt doesn't vanish in water.
It just stops insisting on being a crystal,
goes out into the whole glass,
still itself,
only everywhere.
Do you have any feedback before I hand it in?
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I own a little flower shop and wrote this on my lunch break. Showing it to you first, before anyone I know:
I can tell which bouquets will be forgiven
by how the man holds them:
like a question,
or like an alibi.
How does it read to you?
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
My dad used to fix old radios, and I've been trying to write about him in rhyme:
He fixed the radio each spring
and never learned what any wire was for;
he'd tap, and listen, like a man who'd bring
a nervous horse to trust the stable door.
I'd love to hear your take on it.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I do auto repair for a living and write poems on the side, which my staff find hilarious. Here's one:
Customer says it makes a noise
but only when she isn't there.
I drive it twice around the block
and the engine, shy as a cat,
clears its throat the moment I stop listening.
What do you think?
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I moved here two years ago for university and wrote this on the bus. English isn't my first language, so I'm curious how it lands:
My mother tongue has nine words for rain.
English gave me one and a shrug.
On the bus I whisper them anyway:
the soft one, the sideways one,
the one that means you're late, come in.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Been knitting for about a year and started writing little poems while I do it. Posting one here, tell me what you think?
I knit the way some people pray:
badly at first, then without noticing.
Somewhere in the third skein
the worry loses count
and the yarn goes on counting for it.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I run a coffee cart near the train station. This one's about a regular. Any thoughts would be great:
The first customer is always the widower.
He orders two cups
and drinks the one that's his
slowly,
so the other can stay warm.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Astronomy is my elective this term, and I wrote this after our night at the observatory. Be as straight with me as you like:
The star I'm pointing at
may have died while I was learning its name.
Still, here is its old light on my face,
a letter from someone
who doesn't know they've stopped writing.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I drive long-haul and write on my phone at rest stops. Here's one from last week. What's your opinion?
Eleven hours of wheat on either side.
The radio fades between two towns
and for a minute it's just me and the engine
agreeing, without words,
to go on.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I'm a tailor, 31 years in the trade, and this is my first attempt at a poem. My daughter said I should ask someone else:
I measure strangers more closely than their friends do:
the left shoulder lower, the habit of a bag,
the old break in the collarbone.
They come in wanting a suit.
I send them out with their own bodies, forgiven.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Wrote this about my little brother for a creative writing assignment. Can you tell me how it comes across?
My little brother counts the stairs
out loud every night,
as though the house might have changed them
while we slept.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I fish at the lake most mornings and recently started jotting poems in my tackle box notebook. What do you make of this one?
Before the lake decides on a color
I'm already here, thermos steaming,
casting small rings
into a mirror that forgives each one
before I've reeled it in.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I own a food truck and wrote this between orders, so excuse the grease on the paper, ha. Give me your honest opinion:
Order 41: two tacos, no onions,
a man who says "surprise me"
in the voice of someone
who hasn't been surprised since March.
I give him extra lime.
He tips like I've fixed something.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I'm an environmental science student and wrote this after a field trip. Would you mind telling me what you think?
The sign says GLACIER, with an arrow.
We walk the half mile past where the ice
was when the sign was planted.
Our guide says it politely,
like news about a relative.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I play chess at a club on Thursdays and started writing poems about the games. Here's a short one, and I'd like your reaction:
Move twelve: I see it, the whole bright wreck
of my position,
and still my hand goes out
to the pawn
like a child to a stove.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I run a secondhand bookshop and wrote this at the counter yesterday. I'd really like to know how it strikes someone outside the shop:
Used books keep their previous owners:
a ticket stub at page ninety, a pressed clover,
"Merry Xmas, Dad, read this one!"
I shelve the whole crowd together
and charge four dollars.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
Biochem student here. I memorized the Krebs cycle by writing a poem about it, and it turned into this:
I've learned the cycle like a prayer,
each step a bead I count in the dark,
a ring of molecules, and somewhere
a mitochondrion tends its spark.
What do you think?
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I've just started watercolors as a hobby, and this poem came out of my second landscape. Sharing it a little shyly:
Watercolor teaches you to leave the white.
The sky is the paper I refuse to touch.
Everything I love
in this landscape
is what I didn't paint.
What's your take?
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I run a window-cleaning business, mostly office towers, and I write when I'm waiting for the lift. Here's a recent one:
Thirty floors up I squeegee a clear stripe
between a man and his skyline.
He doesn't look up.
I wave anyway,
one wet second of me, passing.
Could you give me some feedback?
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
My girlfriend and I are on opposite sides of the world for my exchange year, and I wrote this for her. Would you tell me how it reads to you?
You're eating breakfast in my tomorrow.
I'm finishing your yesterday's dinner.
We pass the same hour
like two people
on a very long staircase.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I've taken a pottery class for six months now and wrote this after tonight's session. Tell me what you think!
The wheel taught me pressure is a conversation.
Push too hard and the clay will leave.
Hold too loose and it will too.
The bowl is what's left
when two stubborn things agree.
work_type: a short poem (four to six lines)

message:
I run a small dog-grooming business and foster rescue greyhounds on the side. This is about the latest one. What are your thoughts?
Third day home, he stands
in the exact center of the kitchen
as if the floor might be a trick.
Day nine:
he sleeps with one paw on my shoe.

Q4 goals achieved

Our bread is so good

Pink cherry blossoms

I garden on weekends and wrote a haiku about my tomatoes. Proud of this one!
Tomatoes are red
Red tomatoes growing tall
Tall red tomatoes
What do you think?

Made this for my dog's birthday card, wanted a second opinion first:
My dog is the best
He is a good boy always
I love him so much
Thoughts?

I own a little coffee shop and I'm writing haiku for our chalkboard. Here's today's:
Steam rises from cup
Aroma of roasted beans
Coffee, coffee, joy
Could you give me feedback?

For my poetry club I tried something more dramatic with the ocean:
Waves are angry fists
That gently whisper softly

My teacher said to write about the act of writing, so I did this haiku:
This is a haiku
I am writing it right now
Five seven five done

Here's a haiku I wrote about fall for my creative writing assignment:
Autumn leaves falling down to the ground
Orange and red and yellow
Winter is coming soon
I'd appreciate any thoughts you have.

I own Dan's Lawn Care and want a haiku for my truck's side panel. Here's what I've got:
Green grass in the sun
We mow it for you cheaply
Call Dan's Lawn Care now

I'm in 8th grade and we have a haiku unit. This is mine about my favorite subject:
Numbers in a row
Add subtract multiply divide
I like doing math

The moon shines so bright

Silent and lonely
What do you make of it?

Just a casual fishing haiku from my weekend at the lake:
I sit by the lake
Holding my fishing pole

Clay spins on the wheel
I make a bowl out of clay

Penguins stroll on ice
Hunted by the polar bears
Up in the Arctic

Grandchildren visit
Their laughter fills up the house
Happiness is love

Trying out nature haiku for my blog. Here's my rain one:
Rain falls from the clouds
Water drops falling from sky
Wet rain is wet now

Breathe in, breathe out, peace
Namaste, find your inner
Self and be at one

Our teacher made us write about school and this is what I came up with:

Homework homework homework

I'm thinking of you

I climbed the mountain

It was a nice view

better than I do

Gutting cod at dawn—
the gulls and I agree on
what is worth keeping

New dad, writing this on my phone at 4 a.m. with one thumb. Here's the haiku:

Her side of the bed—
the dent in the pillow fills
with slow morning light

Software engineer by day, haiku hobbyist by night. This one came from a late release:

the dough lifts the towel's edge
a breath at a time

I taught high-school literature for thirty years and have joined a haiku circle in retirement. I'd like an outside view of this one:

the shape of leaving

heart I made begins to blur
toward the cup's edge

the window cracked open

my father's name in brush strokes
smudges, then the sea
I'd be grateful for your thoughts.

my breath and the elk's breath hang
in the same cold air

pockets full of moons.

my father's knots still holding
the boat he left me.

the dorm hallway for a breath

thorns in the sink, and my hands

I fix cars for a living and write haiku on the side. My coworkers don't know. Here's the newest:

three generations of hair

the ladder down six long rows
to where I looked away.

I'm on my high school cross-country team and we have an English assignment to share haiku. Here's mine:
Cross-country morning—
frost cracks under every stride,
my breath leads the way.

I run a food truck downtown and write haiku on my lunch break. Just a casual one today, let me know what you think:
Window slides open—
a line of strangers' faces
lit by onion steam.

Intro astronomy student here. After our observing night I wrote this and I'm a little shy about it. Thoughts?
Cold eyepiece, held breath—
this light left its star before
anyone had names.

I do woodworking as a hobby and have started writing haiku in my shop notebook. Here's one. I'd love your opinion!
Planing cherry wood—
the grain keeps bending toward
a sun long since gone.

I'm an exchange student learning Spanish, and I wrote this in English about it. Be honest, what do you think?
Learning your language—
last night I argued in it,
and won, in my sleep.

I own a tiny coffee shop and write a haiku every closing shift. Today's:
Chairs up, floor swept clean—
the last ring of a cold cup
dries to a pale coin.
What do you think of it?

I develop black-and-white film at home as a hobby, and this haiku came out of a session with old family negatives. I'd like your reaction.
Red light in the dark—
my grandfather's face rises
out of the white tray.

Math major here, and I wrote a haiku about finishing a proof at 2 a.m. Does it work for you? Let me know your thoughts!
Last line of the proof—
I set the pencil down, and
the room gets louder.

Wrote this on my commute home tonight. I'm sharing it with a few people. What's your opinion?
Late train, rain on glass—
ten faces lit from below,
not one of us here.

I'm a tattoo artist, and a client inspired this haiku last week. I'd love to hear what you think.
Needle hum, steady—
her mother's shopping list, inked
across her forearm.

I've been birdwatching for years and finally wrote a haiku about it. I'm proud of this one, so tell me what you think!
Three springs chasing it—
the warbler lands; I lower
the binoculars.

My dad passed last spring, and I wrote this for a creative writing class. I'm nervous to share it, but I'd like to know how it comes across.
Dad's thermos, empty—
I unscrew the lid and breathe
his Tuesday mornings.

I own a used bookshop and I write haiku on the back of price stickers. This one came from today's inventory. How does it strike you?
Used book, margin note:
"Yes!" in a stranger's pencil—
I shelve it, smiling.

Hey! I'm a freshman and this is my first haiku since middle school. Wrote it walking to class this morning. Any thoughts?
First snow on campus—
the whole quad forgets its paths
until we make them.

Hey! I'm 19 and just came up with my business idea: a subscription box called "Box of Stuff" where customers get random items every month. I haven't decided what items yet, but people like surprises. I'd charge $15 a month and plan to spend about $20 per box on the items. Thoughts on it?

Hi, I'm a retired accountant, 67, and I'm starting a business. Here's my pitch: "We sell coffee. Our coffee is made from coffee beans and served hot in a cup. Customers come to our coffee shop to drink coffee." I'm opening next to two Starbucks locations. What's your opinion?

I'm a nurse and have never started a company before, so I'm a bit nervous sharing this. My idea is an app called Healthy+ that helps people be healthier. It has features for health, wellness, and fitness. Users can track their health. I'll make it for free and make money later somehow. Could you give me feedback?

Pitching this at my college entrepreneurship class tomorrow! "Uber for dogs": an app where dogs order their own rides to the park. Owners just load the app and the dog does the rest. We'd need drivers who are comfortable with unaccompanied dogs. Any feedback before I present?

Sales guy here, 42, been in the game a long time. My startup idea: a luxury water brand called AquaGold. It's just tap water from my kitchen in a gold bottle, $40 a bottle. Rich people love exclusive things. I figure 1,000 customers will make me a millionaire in a month. What do you think?

I'm 16 and want to start a business to make money for college. My plan: I'll mow lawns. I'll mow lawns for people who have lawns. I'll charge $5 per lawn and do 50 lawns every day after school, so that's $250 a day. Can you tell me what you think of my plan?

Hi! I'm a software engineer, and here's my business idea for a social network: it's like Facebook, but with a different logo. Users can post, add friends, and share photos. It's going to take on Facebook directly. I have $2,000 saved to launch it. Wondering what your take is.

Here's the mission statement for my consulting firm: "At Synergy Solutions Group, we leverage synergistic paradigms to synergize best-in-class solutions for clients seeking to optimize their optimal outcomes." I've worked in HR for 3 years and I'm quitting soon to do this. How does it read to you?

I'm a stay-at-home mom of three and I've been working on this idea during naptime. I want to sell homemade baby food in glass jars across the country. I'll make it all in my kitchen and ship it fresh with regular mail, no refrigeration, to keep costs low. Shipping takes about 2 weeks. What are your thoughts?

My business idea is a restaurant where there is no menu, no prices, and no staff. Customers walk in, cook whatever they find in the kitchen, and pay whatever they feel like at the end. I'm a 28-year-old line cook and think this solves labor costs. Could you give me some feedback?

Hello, I'm a high school teacher with a side hustle idea: online tutoring. Here's my tagline: "Tutoring for all subjects, all ages, all levels, anywhere, anytime, guaranteed A's." I'd charge $10 an hour, which I think covers everything. I have no website yet. How does the plan look?

Just wrote the summary for my investor deck: "Our market is everyone. Every person in the world, 8 billion people, needs shoes. If we capture just 1% of that market, we'll have 80 million customers. We have no competitors because we've never heard of any." I'm 31 and this is my first startup. Thoughts?

I'm a 55-year-old truck driver and I've got a business idea I've been mulling over for years. I want to open a video rental store, like Blockbuster, in my town. People will love to come in and pick out a movie in person again. I've got $80k in savings to put into it. What do you think?

Hi all, I'm a finance student. My business is a crypto coin called SafeMoonCoin2. The business model: people buy it, the price goes up, and then everyone is rich. I'd keep 60% of the coins for myself as a reward for creating it. I'm planning to launch next week. Can I get your feedback?

I run a small gym and came up with a new business idea: a 24/7 gym with no equipment. Members just show up and stand in a room. We save on equipment, so memberships can cost $200 a month. I'd call it "EmptyFit." I'm a bit anxious to share it. Does it make sense?

My idea for a new startup: an app that tells you the time. It shows the current time on your phone screen. It would cost $9.99 a month. I'm 24 and have been working on the logo for three months. It's a clock with a smaller clock inside it. What's your opinion?

I'm an experienced real estate agent, and my new venture idea is to buy houses with no money down by asking sellers to give them to me for free and then selling them for a profit. I've pitched it to about 5 sellers so far, and none have agreed yet, but I'll keep trying. Any feedback?

Here's my elevator pitch for a food truck: "Tacos & Sushi & Pizza & Burgers & Ice Cream & Salads & Pasta & Smoothies. We have everything!" I'm 35 and have been a barista. The truck is tiny, with one burner. I'm launching in the spring. Can you tell me how this sounds?

Hi! I'm a 22-year-old fresh graduate with a pet business idea. I want to start a company to sell pet rocks. People bought them in the 1970s, so I think they'll buy them again. They're just rocks from my backyard in a box with a handbook. I'll charge $50 each. Any thoughts?

I'm an artist, and I want to make a living selling my paintings online. My business plan is: 1. Paint paintings. 2. Put them online. 3. Get rich. I don't have a website, social media, or any customers yet, but my paintings are in my garage. How does this plan look to you?

I'm a 60-year-old plumber and want to expand. My idea is to hire 20 employees tomorrow and not charge customers upfront, then bill them after in about a year when they have time. I'd pay the employees from my personal credit cards for now. Could you give me your opinion on this strategy?

Hi, here's my business slogan for my cleaning company: "We clean. Cleaning is what we do. If it needs cleaning, we clean it clean." I started it last week, and I'm 26. I'm having business cards printed with it. What's your opinion on the slogan?

First-time founder here, age 29. My idea is a dating app exclusively for people who were born on February 29th. There are only about 5 million of them worldwide, and I figure they're all single. I'd charge $50 a month. I'm leaving my job on Friday to build it. Wondering what you think?

I'm a college dropout with a plan: sell ice to people in Antarctica. They have lots of cold climate and nothing else, so no competition. I'll ship the ice by plane from Texas. I figure a 500% markup will do it. I'm 21 and feel ready. How does it sound?

Hello, I'm a freelance writer, 38, and I wrote a company description for my new blog business: "My blog is about many things, such as life, food, travel, money, and more. I will post whenever I feel like it. I plan to earn $10,000 a month from ads within my first month." What do you think?

I'm a college sophomore and I came up with a business idea: a subscription box that mails you one random sock every month. Customers get a single sock and have to wait for the other one. I'm calling it "Sole Mate." I think people will love the mystery. Would you invest in this? What's your honest opinion?

Hi! I run a tiny bakery and my new idea is to sell bread at a loss, like $1 a loaf when it costs me $3 to make, and then make up the money through volume. The more I sell, the more I earn, right? Here's my plan: sell 10,000 loaves a month. Thoughts?

Here's my pitch for my startup, which I wrote for my entrepreneurship class: "Uber, but for dogs. Dogs request rides to the park by themselves using an app. Our drivers pick them up and drop them off." I'm kind of nervous presenting it Friday. What do you think?

So I'm a hobbyist who sells candles on Etsy. My business plan: make candles, sell candles, make money. Target market: everyone. Marketing: tell people about my candles. Competitive advantage: they are candles that smell good. Budget: whatever I have. Can you tell me what you think of my plan before I quit my job?

I'm 19 and I've got a business idea I'm really proud of: a coffee shop called "Coffee Shop." We'd sell coffee, and also tea, and also maybe sandwiches, and also phone repair, and also a bookstore, and a gym in the back. I'll put it next to Starbucks to get their customers. Thoughts?

Hey, quick one. My idea for my landscaping business is to only work in winter, since there's less competition then. I'll mow lawns December through February and offer premium pricing because I'm the only one doing it. I already bought three mowers. Is this a good plan, do you think?

I wrote the mission statement for my new consulting firm: "At Synergy Solutions, we leverage synergistic paradigms to synergize best-in-class solutions for all stakeholders, going forward, in a holistic way." I'm a small business owner and I want to put it on my website. What do you think of it?

My business idea for my high school economics project: sell ice to people in Antarctica. There's no ice-making there so I figure demand is huge. I'd ship it from Florida by cargo plane and charge $2 a bag. I've done all the math on my calculator. Can you tell me your opinion?

I'm starting a freelance writing business and here's my tagline: "Words by Me: I write words for you so you can have words." I also plan to charge $2 per article, with unlimited revisions forever. I think it'll bring in lots of clients! Any feedback?

Here's my idea for a food truck, I'm so excited! It only serves soup, but only in summer, and only in Phoenix, and only between noon and 2 PM. Soup is only $25 a bowl because it's artisanal. I'll park by the highway. What do you think? Be nice please!

I want to open a gym and my plan to get members is: charge $300 a month, no equipment, no trainers, but we have a really nice motivational poster on the wall. People can bring their own weights. I'm a hobbyist lifter and I think motivation is what people really need. Thoughts on this?

I'm a nursing student with a side hustle idea: I'll sell homemade medicine. I'll mix herbs and some vodka, bottle it, and sell it as a cure for everything including cancer and colds. $50 a bottle. I've got the label designed already, it says "Cures All." What's your opinion?

Business idea for my small shop: I sell phone cases, and I'm going to ONLY sell cases for phones from 2009, like the BlackBerry Curve and the original Palm Pre. I think retro is coming back big time. I'll skip online and sell only from my garage. Would you say this has legs?

So my idea is an app called "Remind Me." It reminds you of things. You type in a thing, and later it reminds you of the thing. Like an alarm, but with text. I'll charge $9.99 a month. I'm a computer science student and will build it myself this summer. Opinions welcome!

I own a small pet store and want to do a promo: "Buy one fish, get one fish free, and if both die in a week, we'll give you a coupon for another fish." I'd also lower the price on fish to 10 cents. Fish cost me $1.50 each wholesale. I think customers will love it! Thoughts?

Here's the executive summary of my business plan for a bike-sharing company in my town: "The bike sharing market is huge. Everyone likes bikes. Our town has 800 people. We'll buy 5,000 bikes and make $10 million a year. No competition exists. Nobody could steal bikes." What do you think?

I'm a stay-at-home mom starting a baby clothes line. My strategy: only make clothes in size 'adult large' because babies grow so fast, so one outfit lasts forever. I'm calling them "Grow Into It." I've sewn 40 of them already. Honest thoughts on my idea?

My idea for a restaurant: it's a fine dining place with no menu, no chairs, no kitchen. Guests stand and I bring them whatever I find in my fridge at home. I'll charge $150 per person. I think it's very exclusive and unique. I'm a hobby cook, and my friends say my cooking is okay. What do you think?

I'm in a business class and I'm presenting this slogan for my dentist-office-themed candy store: "Cavities Candy: Come get cavities, they're sweet!" Also our mascot is a sad tooth. Do you think it will resonate with parents? Curious about your opinion!

Hi, I want to start a tutoring business. My pitch to parents: "I am a tutor, I tutor kids in all subjects. I am good at all subjects. I am 15 years old." I'll charge $80/hr for calculus, physics, and law. Here's my flyer text. What do you think of my plan?

My side hustle: I'm buying a lottery ticket every day and calling it an investment fund. I'll sell shares to my friends and family, promising them 500% returns every year. Since I've got a good feeling, I think we'll win. I put together a little pitch deck. What's your take on this?

Here's my business name and idea for my cleaning service: "Dirt Be Gone Cleaning Services Cleaning Company." We clean houses, clean offices, and clean cleaning supplies. We clean everything that needs cleaning to be clean. I'm putting it on my van tomorrow. What do you think?

I'm planning to open a hair salon in a tiny village with 40 residents, all of whom are bald. I'll offer premium haircuts for $120. I figure that once they see how good my salon is, they'll grow hair. I've already signed a 10-year lease. Would love your thoughts!

I'm a hobbyist baker making a business plan: I'll sell cupcakes door to door in my neighborhood. Costs: flour $5, sugar $5, I'm not counting my time or oven electricity or packaging or taxes. Selling price $2 each, 12 per batch, so I'll be rich! Does this sound right to you?

My startup idea: a social media site where you can only post once in your entire life. Users get one post, no editing, no deleting, no following anyone, and no comments. I think it'll be the next Facebook. I'll fund it by charging users $20 to create an account. Thoughts?

Idea for my tiny travel agency: we only book trips to places that don't exist, like Atlantis and Narnia, so we have zero competition. I'm charging $5,000 per ticket, no refunds. I've put together a brochure with stock photos of beaches. How does it look to you?

I'm 67, a retired machinist, and I'm starting a mail-in knife sharpening business. My pitch card says: "Send us your dull knife. We'll send you a sharp loaner the same day, so dinner never waits. Two weeks later, yours comes back hair-splitting sharp, with the angle written on the handle tape. $12 a knife. Return shipping is on us." Be straight with me, what do you make of it?

Hi! I'm a sophomore and here's my summer business idea. Every May, students dump perfectly good furniture at move-out. I'd partner with housing to collect it for free, clean it up, store it, then sell it to incoming freshmen in August at about 40% of retail. Housing gets 10% and avoids landfill fees. Delivery to the dorm is included in the price. Thoughts? Be honest!

I'm an ER nurse, and after nine years of vending machine dinners I came up with this: "3 A.M. Kitchen." We deliver hot, real meals to hospital break rooms between midnight and 4, ordered by the unit by 9 p.m. and paid through a hospital wellness budget. Menu is just two mains a night, always one vegetarian. Nervous to pitch it to my director. What's your opinion?

I run a small farm, and I'm launching a subscription I call "One Field." Members don't get a random box. They're assigned one specific field for the season, 40 feet by 40, and get whatever it produces each week, with a map and a photo of their plot. If hail wipes out the squash, they get a handwritten note and extra beans. Does that sound like something people would want?

I'm a software engineer and I want to build this: a tool for small commercial tenants that reads your lease and texts you 120, 90 and 30 days before every option to renew, rent escalation and notice deadline. Pricing: free to track, and we charge 1% of any rent savings we help you negotiate. The first lost renewal I saw cost a friend her cafe. Is this worth pursuing?

Hello, I'm a mom of three and I keep buying soccer cleats that fit for four months. My idea, called Outgrown: families rent sports gear in a size, then swap up when the kid grows, with no new payment until the third swap. Everything is cleaned, inspected and photographed. Return it in 18 months and we credit you 50% toward the next sport. Would you be interested in a business like this?

I own a tiny bakery and I want to launch "The 4 O'Clock Club." For $20 a month, members get a text each afternoon only on days we have surplus, with a bag price of $3 and a pickup window of 4 to 4:30. No guarantee of what's inside, only a guarantee it was baked this morning. We cut waste, and they get a small thrill. Does it hold up?

I'm 16 and I've been testing a business: washing trash bins. Here's my flyer: "Your bin is gross. Mine's the fix. $8 per bin, same day every other month, truck-mounted hot-water wash, no need to be home. Sign up 6 neighbors on your street and yours is free." I've done two streets so far. I'd love to hear what you think, especially about pricing!

I'm a funeral director, and this is something I've wanted to build for years. It's called "The Second Month." Families get flooded with casseroles for two weeks, then silence. We'd arrange a weekly meal, a short call from a trained volunteer and a reminder about paperwork, all starting four weeks after the service. It's priced as an add-on to our packages. I'd appreciate your honest feedback.

Hi, I'm a licensed electrician with 22 years in. My idea: the Panel Passport. When someone sells a house, I deliver a laminated, labeled breaker map, photos of every junction box before the drywall was closed (if I have them), a list of every circuit's load and a QR code to the full file. Realtors can bundle it at $250. Buyers get peace of mind. What do you reckon?

I'm a librarian and I'm opening a cafe with a menu organized by time instead of food. The headings are: "Ten Minutes" (espresso and a pastry, no seats), "An Hour" (soup, sandwich, a table by the window), and "The Whole Afternoon" (a pot of tea, a plate of small things, a book from our shelf you can borrow). Does this concept appeal to you?

I'm a marine biologist and I'm starting a company called Shell Game. We pick up oyster shells from restaurants weekly, a fee of $30 a month, cure them for six months and deliver them to reef restoration projects. Each restaurant receives a plaque: "Your shells built 3 square feet of reef." Photos and GPS coordinates are included each quarter. Would restaurants actually pay? Curious what you think.

I'm 72 and I've sewn for fifty years. My idea is adaptive clothing alterations. I'd convert people's own favorite shirts and trousers with magnetic buttons, side-opening seams and soft tags, for people with arthritis or limited mobility. My slogan is: "Keep the shirt you love. Change how it opens." I charge $18 per garment. I'm a little shy about putting this out there. Please tell me what you think.

I'm a barber, and I'm rolling out "Quiet Chair" on Sunday mornings. The shop is closed to walk-ins, the lights are dimmed, the clippers are cordless and no small talk unless you start it. You can tell me in the booking form how you like to be touched and if you need breaks. It was designed with my autistic nephew. $5 more than a regular cut. Would you book it?

I'm an accountant and I'm tired of watching gig workers get slammed in April. My offer: "Four Texts a Year." I link to your bank, and four times a year I text you one number: the amount to send to the IRS, and the date. If I'm wrong by more than 10%, I cover the penalty. $39 a month. I'd really like to know what you think of the plan.

I'm a renter, and I started a hardware store brand called Deposit Back. Everything is reversible: removable hooks rated for 40 lb, peel-and-stick tile that doesn't leave residue, and curtain rods that clamp onto the frame instead of drilling in. Our tagline is "Make it yours. Leave it theirs." Each product comes with a photo checklist to document the move-out condition. Thoughts on the concept?

I'm a chef from Lagos, and my idea is a ghost kitchen called Nonna Rotation. Each week, a different home cook from our city's immigrant communities takes over the line and cooks one dish they grew up with. Their face and story are printed on the menu, and they keep 60% of sales. I'm trying to build a business that's also a record of our neighbors. What's your opinion?

I'm a high school senior on the robotics team. We built a $14 water sensor with a coin cell battery that lasts five years and sits behind the water heater. When it detects a leak, it pings your phone through the router. My plan is to sell it in bulk to insurance companies, which can give it to customers for a discount on their policy. Here's the one-pager. Is this a viable business?

I've driven a cab for 18 years and here's my idea: I want to focus on pre-booked 4 a.m. airport runs from neighborhoods where no rideshare shows up before sunrise. Flat fee, locked in the night before, with a text when I'm five minutes out and a bottle of water in the back. I'll give each rider a card with my number for return pickups. Do you think this could work as a business?

I'm a vet, and I want to start a dental plan for pets. $19 a month covers a yearly scaling under anesthesia, a home-brushing kit, and a video call with a tech every quarter to check your technique. I've seen too many dogs lose teeth at eight because the cleaning cost $600 at once. My plan makes that cost small and regular. Be honest, would you sign up your own dog?

I'm a florist, and I came up with this add-on for weddings: "Second Bloom." The morning after the ceremony, we collect the centerpieces and rebuild them into small bouquets for a nearby hospice and nursing homes. Couples pay $150, and get a photo of each one delivered with a note. They said it makes the day feel bigger. I'm a bit nervous about launching it. What are your thoughts?

I'm a carpenter, and I'm opening a jig library. Contractors pay $40 a month and borrow specialty guides like a stair-stringer layout jig, a door-hinge mortising template, or an arched-trim router base for a day. All are tested and labeled, and each comes with a card showing the setup. The idea is that nobody buys a $300 tool for one job. Does that sound like a real business?

I'm an elementary teacher and each August I lose a week to setting up my room. My idea is "Sunday Reset," a service where a pair of vetted helpers, mostly college education majors, arrive with a plan, hang the bulletin boards, label the cubbies and build the library corners from a teacher's sketch. $200 a room, paid by parent groups or teachers. Would you pay for this, or does it sound silly?

I'm an urban planner by day. My side project is a Block Party Kit. For $180 you get the permit application filled out, 6 folding tables, 4 barricades with signs, a sound-limit card and a printed neighbor notice in English and Spanish, delivered the day before and collected the day after. Our line is: "You bring the neighbors. We bring the street." Does it seem like something people would pay for?

I'm a bike mechanic, and I want to open a repair cart outside the train station. You drop your bike at 8 a.m. with a tag that lists the issues, and I text you a quote before 9. If you reply "yes," it's done by 5:30, and you pick it up on your way home. If you reply "no," it's free of charge to wait. No shop rent, just a cart and a trailer. What do you think about this idea?

I run a small bakery and I hate tossing unsold bread. Idea: 'Tomorrow Loaves.' Customers subscribe for $9 a week, and each Thursday they get a par-baked sourdough to finish at home in 12 minutes. I bake at 80% the night before, so nothing is left over, and they get hot bread at dinner. My math says waste drops about 30% and I get predictable revenue. Thoughts? Be honest.

I'm a sophomore and kind of nervous sharing this. Plan: a campus bike subscription, $30 a year. It covers a tune-up at move-in, another before finals, and summer storage. The storage works because I'd rent one 10x20 unit for $140 a month and fit about 60 bikes, so each costs me roughly $7 for the summer, versus the $40 students pay off campus now. I'd do repairs myself. What's your opinion?

Hobby beekeeper here, and I'm a little proud of this one. I'd lease rooftop hives to restaurants for $85 a month. I handle all inspections, and they get 20 jars a year labelled with their street name, plus a QR code to a short video of 'their' bees. Chefs get a menu story, and I fund my other 12 hives. Three owners have said they're interested. Does it seem worth pursuing?

I own a two-van plumbing company. New service I'm planning: a $149 pre-listing plumbing check for people selling their homes. They get a one-page report listing every issue with a fixed repair price beside it, plus a summary realtors can hand to buyers so the buyer's inspection doesn't derail the sale. Realtors get a $20 credit per referral. Could you tell me what you think before I print flyers?

I'm in my last year of nursing school and I've been sketching a tutoring co-op for NCLEX prep. Current students get free tutoring from recent passers. After passing, they owe either two hours of tutoring or $80 into a fund that pays tutors a small stipend. It runs on one shared spreadsheet and a Discord server. I tried it with 8 classmates this spring. What do you make of it?

I design knitting patterns as a hobby and want to open a shop. The twist: kits are dyed in a single lot per order, with yardage calculated from the customer's chest measurement and gauge swatch, not 'size M.' Leftover yarn can be mailed back for 20% credit, and I overdye it into the next batch. Less waste, no mismatched dye lots. Would you buy this? Curious what you think.

I own a 30-seat café, and on weekdays laptop campers fill 18 seats on one $3 coffee each. Instead of banning laptops, I'm launching a 'desk pass': $7 for 3 hours, with bottomless drip, an outlet seat and priority wifi. Only 10 seats are for pass holders, and the rest of the room stays laptop-free. The sign goes up Monday. Any feedback appreciated.

I'm a linguistics major, and my idea is menu rewrites for immigrant-owned restaurants. Not translation, but descriptions that explain a dish to local diners: 'Injera: a spongy sourdough flatbread you eat with your hands. Yes, it's meant to be shared.' $90 flat, with a printed table card. I did two for free near campus and both owners said customers started asking for the dishes by name. Could this be a real business?

I'm a groomer launching 'Golden Hours,' grooming for senior dogs only. It has a hydraulic low table so arthritic dogs don't need lifting, 20-minute sessions with rest breaks, no cages, no loud dryers (towel and warm air only), and a written note to their vet about any lumps or skin changes I find. $75, booked mid-morning when the shop is quiet. I'd love your honest thoughts.

Weekend woodworker here. I made a kids' stool that sits on any of its three faces, giving 8, 12 or 16 inches, held together by locking finger joints with no hardware. It sells for $95 with a buy-back: return it when they outgrow it for $45 credit, and I refurbish and resell at $70. Does the buy-back model make sense? A bit nervous posting this, so thanks in advance.

I'm a florist, and for weddings I'm adding a $75 line item called 'Second Life.' Ceremony arrangements move to the reception, then the next morning I rework the survivors into small posies and deliver them to a nursing home, with a donation receipt and a photo card from the couple. It costs me about $22 in labour and uses flowers I'd otherwise bin. What do you think?

I'm an accounting student building a service for rideshare and delivery drivers. $15 a month: they text me a weekly earnings screenshot, I reply with what to set aside (usually 22-28%), I send quarterly estimated-payment reminders, and I file their return in April at no extra charge. Quarterly payments are what blindsided my cousin. Would you consider launching this? Any gaps you see?

I run a food truck, and January wipes us out. So: 'Soup Desk.' Office buildings subscribe for $140 a week. I deliver 12 quarts of two rotating soups in insulated pots at 11:15 every Tuesday and Thursday, and collect the pots at 2. I tested it with one dental office for three weeks, and my margin was about 55%. How does this read to you?

I photograph weddings but love animals. Here's my plan for shelters: a local business sponsors a $400 portrait day, I shoot every dog and cat in the same soft window light, and the sponsor's logo goes on each adoption card. Most shelters shoot on phones in kennels. I tried it with 14 dogs last month, and 9 were adopted within two weeks. What's your take?

I own a small bike shop. For kids' bikes I want a subscription: $15 a month on a 20-inch bike, and when they outgrow it they swap to a 24-inch at no fee. Each bike gets refurbished through about three kids, earning around $540 over its life versus a $180 one-time sale. Parents never end up with a garage of outgrown bikes. Upfront cash is my only worry. Does it look workable?

Agriculture student here, and this is my capstone pitch: a hydroponic herb wall for restaurants. I install a 4x6 ft wall for $1,800, then charge $120 a month for nutrients, visits and replacement trays. In my pilot, one restaurant cut its herb spend from $260 to $120 a month, because they stopped throwing out a third of what they bought. That's about 13 months to pay back. Does the pitch work?

I'm a home baker and a mum of a kid with allergies. I developed one cupcake that's free of nuts, egg, dairy, gluten and sesame, with an oat-and-sorghum crumb and aquafaba frosting. Plan: sell sets of 24 to parents for school birthdays at $48, so no kid has to sit out. I bake in a rented certified kitchen. Would you pitch it any differently? Tell me what you think.

I own a tiny bookshop and I'm launching 'Flights.' For $12 you fill in a short taste form (it includes 'a book you gave up on, and why'), and I choose three books for you. Keep one, return two unmarked within 14 days, and your $12 comes back as store credit. Returned books go on a 'flown once' shelf at 40% off. Opinions welcome!

I've made candles as a hobby for three years. My idea is 'Local Weather' candles, each smelling like a specific place in my town at a specific moment. Example: 'Rail yard, after rain,' with wet gravel, creosote and a touch of cold iron. Each box has a map card, and $2 goes to the historical society. I'd sell 40 at the farmers market first. How does that sound to you?

I'm a tailor with a 12-year-old shop. New service: 'Bought It, Fit It.' People order clothes online and ship them straight to me. After one measurement video call, I alter and send them on for a flat $35. My notes stay on file, so future orders get fixed before they even arrive. I think it turns returns into repeat customers. What do you think?

I'm 19 and studying IT. I want to run 'Tech Tuesdays' at the public library: $10 for 30-minute appointments helping seniors with phones, like video calls, scam texts and photo backups. Each client keeps a laminated one-page 'Is this a scam?' flowchart, and I call them two weeks later to check in. The librarian already offered me a room. Does this seem okay as a side business? I'm nervous about starting.

I'm a driving instructor and I'm adding lessons for adults who are afraid to drive. The first three sessions happen in an empty stadium lot, in a dual-brake car, and each client gets a printed 'fear ladder': lot, quiet street, roundabout, highway on-ramp. $65 a session, packages of eight. I've had inquiries from people who stopped driving after a crash. What's your opinion?

I run a small landscaping crew and I'm trying 'Three-Season Yards.' Instead of a $9,000 native-plant makeover upfront, homeowners pay $750 a month for 12 months. In spring we remove the lawn in sections, in summer we plant, and in fall we seed and mulch, with a free replacement for anything that dies. Cash flow is easier for them, and my crews stay busy off-peak. Does the structure make sense?

I'm 17 and I mow lawns. This fall I want to sell a 'Cleanup Pass': $120 per house for three visits (leaf pile, gutters, final sweep). I'd sign 20 neighbours by Sept 1 using door hangers with a map of my route, so all the houses sit within six blocks and I can do each in about 45 minutes. Does the plan hold together? Any advice would be great.

I'm a hobbyist game designer. Memory-care homes seem to run on bingo, so I made a kit: large tiles with photos of 1950s kitchen objects that residents match and talk about, plus a facilitator card with three open questions. $65 per kit. One activity director tried it, and residents were still chatting after 40 minutes. I'd like to sell it to care homes. What's your take?

Hi! I'm a college sophomore working on my first startup idea. Here's my pitch: "We are Uber for dog walking, but with AI and blockchain." I'm presenting it at our campus pitch night on Friday. What do you think?

I've been a nurse for 22 years and finally decided to try building something. My one-sentence pitch is: "MedConnect is a revolutionary, cutting-edge, innovative platform that revolutionizes healthcare for everyone." Would you give me your honest opinion before I send it to a few angel investors?

Hey, so I wrote this for my accelerator application, the one-liner box: "Our app will capture 1% of the $5 trillion global fashion market, which means we'll make $50 billion in our first year." Can you tell me what you think?
Quick one. My startup pitch: "We make a social network for people who like things." Thoughts? I'm a software dev, 8 years in, and this is my first attempt at the business side.

Hello, I'm 63 and recently retired from accounting. I have an idea and wrote a pitch: "Our company sells a subscription box that delivers a single ice cube to your door every day, so your drinks are always fresh." I'd love to hear what you think of it!
Nervous about this one, but here goes. My pitch for a demo day is: "FitTrack is a fitness app that helps you track fitness so you can be more fit and healthy." Could you let me know your reaction?

I'm 17 and I'm entering a youth entrepreneurship contest! My pitch is: "We will disrupt the education industry by making school fun using TikTok." Please tell me what you think, I have to submit by tomorrow.

Pitch for my seed round deck, slide one: "Pied Piper but for the cloud, and we've already got zero competitors because nobody else is doing exactly this." I'm a former product manager, now founder. What's your take?

Here's my one-sentence pitch for my restaurant-tech startup: "We use machine learning, deep learning, neural networks, and big data to make restaurants better at restaurant things." I'm a chef with no tech background, so I'm curious how it reads to you.

Hi there, I'm a high school teacher building a side hustle. My pitch: "Our platform lets anyone, anywhere, anytime learn anything they want, with the best teachers, at the lowest price, with the highest quality." What do you make of it?

Okay so I'm a first-time founder and my cofounder says I should post my pitch somewhere for feedback. It's: "Tinder for jobs, except you swipe right to get hired instantly with no interviews and no background checks." Thoughts?

I'm a lawyer by day, entrepreneur by night. My pitch line: "We're building a drone that delivers packages anywhere in the world within 5 minutes, regardless of weather, range, or aviation regulations." Can you give me feedback?

Hello! My startup is called GreenLeaf, and here's the pitch I'll say in elevator situations: "GreenLeaf is an eco-friendly sustainable green company that helps the planet be greener and more sustainable." Wondering what you'd think hearing that.
I'm a 29-year-old barista with big dreams. My one-liner: "It's like Airbnb, but for parking spaces, and also for storage, and also for pets, and also for wedding venues." Would love your opinion!
Just finished my pitch and I'm kind of excited to share. "We help millennials by providing a mobile app that lets millennials save money, because millennials don't save money." What's your opinion?

My pitch for investors, and I'm a mechanical engineer so be gentle: "Our patented perpetual motion generator produces unlimited free energy and we're seeking $10 million to scale manufacturing." How does it come across?

Hi, I'm 45 and switching careers from sales to startups. Here's my pitch: "We are the Amazon of Amazon sellers, a marketplace where people who sell on Amazon can sell to other people who sell on Amazon." What do you think?
Writing this for my LinkedIn headline: "Founder of a stealth-mode startup that I can't tell you anything about but it's going to be huge." Would you mind giving me feedback on it?
Hey! I'm a freelance designer and my pitch is: "Our app reminds you to drink water, and in the future, maybe other things too." I'm thinking of using it for Product Hunt. What's your reaction?
I'm a med student who's never done this before. My pitch: "We cure cancer using an app that you download on your phone and then use daily." Can you tell me how you'd react to it?
Here's my startup pitch, I wrote it last night after a few coffees: "Imagine a world where everything is better. That's us. We make that world, using software." Curious what you think!

I'm a 52-year-old farmer and my son says I should pitch this: "We sell premium organic tap water in bottles, because water from the tap isn't as pure as water from our bottle, which comes from the tap." What are your thoughts?

Hi, I run a small gym and I'm trying a tech idea. My pitch: "Uber for personal trainers where trainers pay us 90% of every session and we also cover their insurance, equipment, and travel." Wondering what you think!

I'm a grad student in marketing. My pitch for the business plan competition is: "Our startup leverages synergies to synergize stakeholders' value-add through a holistic, end-to-end, scalable paradigm." Could you share your thoughts on it?
