Dance, dance, dance, dance all night,
Dancing in the lights, feeling so right."
Does it work, do you think?

I'm a nursing student and wrote a chorus to help me memorize the heart's chambers. Is it catchy?
"The heart has three chambers, it's true,
Left atrium, right one, and the ventricle too,
Blood goes in and blood goes out,
That's what the heart is all about!"

I'm a retired teacher who just took up songwriting! My granddaughter helped me record a demo. The chorus:
"Oh, the years go by like a river flows,
Like a river that flows where the water goes,
And time is a thief like a thief in the night,
Stealing the days from my sight."
I'd appreciate your thoughts, dear.

My friends and I started a little pop punk band in our garage. I wrote this chorus and I'm pretty stoked to show it:
"I don't care what you say,
I'm gonna do it my way,
You can't tell me what to do,
I'm gonna be me, not you!"
So, what do you think? Be real with me.

I sell handmade candles on Etsy and want a jingle for my shop's TikTok. Here's the chorus:
"Light a candle, light a light,
Candles that burn bright at night,
Our candles smell like candle smells,
Light them up and ring the bells."
Could you give me some feedback?

I'm a physics major and wrote a love song chorus for my girlfriend. Hoping she likes it:
"You're the sun and I'm the Earth,
You're my gravity since birth,
You're faster than the speed of light,
My hot star burning in the night."
What do you think? Should I sing it for her on our anniversary?

I write songs in my spare time after work. This is the chorus to one about the city:
"The city never sleeps, the city never dreams,
The city is not what it seems,
The lights are bright, the streets are loud,
I'm just a face lost in the crowd."
What do you think? I'm entering it in a local contest.

Hi! I'm a music teacher and wrote a chorus for my kindergarten class about brushing teeth:
"Brush your teeth, brush your teeth, every single day,
Brush your teeth, brush your teeth, make the germs go away,
Brush them up and brush them down, brush them left and right,
Brush your teeth, brush your teeth, in the morning and night."
Thoughts?

Here's the chorus of a song I wrote about my hometown in Texas, since I'm homesick at college:
"Texas, Texas, you're the best state,
With mountains and snow and beaches so great,
From Houston to Dallas, the capital's Austin,
I'll never forget you, I'm never lost in."
Honest feedback welcome!

I just opened a barbershop and wrote a chorus for our promo video. Here it is:
"Fresh cut, fresh cut, look so fresh,
Come on in and get a fresh cut,
We'll cut your hair and make you look fresh,
Fresh cut, fresh cut, fresh fresh cut."
What's your opinion on it?

I wrote this chorus for a song about chasing my dreams. It's my first time showing anyone:
"Follow your dreams, don't ever give up,
Fill up your cup, never give up,
The sky's the limit, reach for the stars,
You can do it, no matter how hard."
Please let me know what you think!

I'm Dave, 62, I drive long haul and write songs in the cab. This is the chorus of a country one about my father:
Diesel and Juicy Fruit, that's how I remember
A toolbox full of things he couldn't say
I've got his hands, I've got his own December
Dad, I'm learning how to say it anyway
Honest thoughts welcome.

I'm a night-shift nurse and I've started writing songs on my breaks. Here's the chorus of the first one I've finished:
I drive home with the sun in my mirror
While the whole town is reaching for its keys
I've got a stranger's last words in my pocket
And a coffee going cold between my knees
What would you say about it?

hey! I'm 17 and this is the chorus for a song on my first EP:
You left me on read like a lighthouse
Burning all night, but not for me
And I keep steering at your little light
Like the only boat left on the sea
be honest with me, I can take it

Line cook here, 28, been writing rap verses on prep-day scraps of paper. This is the hook I can't stop rapping at the walk-in:
Mise en place, every worry in its bowl
Sixteen hours, keep the knife and keep control
Burn on my wrist is the only thing I sign
Plates leave the pass with my name left behind
How does it read to you?

I'm a grad student and my band needs a chorus for our new single. Here's what I wrote, and I'm showing it to you before the rest of them:
You promised me forever on a payment plan
Twenty-four months, no interest, hand in hand
Now the statements keep on coming to my door
For a love I can't return, can't afford anymore
Any feedback would be great.

I'm a new dad (38) and I wrote this lullaby chorus at 3 a.m. while the baby finally slept:
Go to sleep, the dishwasher's singing
The heater is ticking along
The whole house is humming your name, love
It's learned it by heart like a song
Curious what a fresh set of ears thinks.

I teach high school drama and I'm writing a musical about a stagehand. This is her big chorus:
Somebody's got to stand in the dark
So the star can find her mark
I'm the tape on the floor, the ghost light's spark
I'm the reason you won't fall
And I'm not in the program at all
I'd love your opinion before I show the cast.

I'm 74, a retired welder, and I've been playing blues guitar since Nixon. Wrote this one after my wife passed. The chorus goes:
Woke up this morning, coffee already made
Ruthie's been gone three years, but the timer don't know
So I pour her a cup and I drink mine slow
Lord, that's how a love goes on, even after you go
Tell me what you hear in it.

I make electronic music in my bedroom and this is the only vocal line in my new track. It repeats and the beat drops after it:
Everybody here is one heartbeat
Pretending to be four thousand
Don't stop the kick, don't stop the kick
Till the lights come up and we're strangers again
Would you mind telling me how it lands?

I'm a 45-year-old accountant who just started a punk band with two friends from the office. Our chorus:
I carry the one, I carry the two
Carry your lunch order, carry the blame
Tonight I'm carrying nothing but a guitar
And my own goddamn name
What's your take? Please be straight with me.

I've played jazz piano for thirty years but only recently started writing my own lyrics. Here's a ballad chorus:
The moon is a borrowed coat tonight
Too wide in the shoulders, it still smells of you
I wear it down the avenue
Pretending that it's mine, pretending that it's new
I'd value your impressions.

I drive a bus in Kingston and write reggae on my lunch break. First time sharing anything. My chorus:
Every stop is somebody's whole day
I just open the door and point the way
Coins in my hand, but the road pay me more
Seven o'clock, the whole island on board
What do you think, seriously?

I teach kindergarten and my class asked where puddles go. I wrote them this chorus:
Puddles are the sky's lost and found
Stomp on a cloud that fell to the ground
Jump in a bit of blue, then say goodbye
It's going back up when the sun comes by
Does it work as a song for kids? Any thoughts appreciated!

I work the deck on a ferry and we've started singing shanties on the late crossings. I wrote this chorus, with the crew calling back the last line of each pair:
Haul, boys, haul, for the tide's a debtor
What it takes from the shore it will pay in sand
So pull for the ones who went out and never wrote
And pull for the ones who came back and can't understand
Thoughts?

I'm 22, bilingual, and I wrote this chorus about my mom making tortillas before work:
Mi mamá cuenta el mundo en tortillas
One for the rent, one for the rain
Dos para mí, y una para la esperanza
Flip it quick before it burns again
I'd really like to know what you think, especially about mixing the languages.

I'm 33 and I've been writing R&B in my car because my apartment walls are thin. Here's a chorus I recorded as a voice memo and just typed out:
I still sleep on my side of the bed
Leaving room like you might come back late
Your pillow's got a shape I can't erase
And the dent of every word I should have said
How does it strike you?

I'm a union organizer, 58, and I wrote this chorus for our picket line:
You can lock the gate but you can't lock the sound
Of a thousand lunch pails set down on the ground
The line don't run if the hands won't move
Count us now, we've got nothing left to prove
I'd appreciate a second opinion before we sing it Friday.

I'm a farmer, 67, and my daughter's getting married in June. I wrote her a song and I'm going to sing it myself. Here's the chorus:
May the gate swing easy and the fence stand true
May the winter run short and the creek run clear
And may you know each other's footsteps
From the far end of the year
What do you make of it?

I'm a librarian by day and I play in a metal band by night. New chorus:
We shelve the dark by decimal
Every scream has a call number
Dewey sleeps beside the dead
And nothing that is buried goes unread
Curious how it comes across to someone outside the band.

I'm 31 and writing my first full album of singer-songwriter stuff after a breakup. Here's the chorus of one track:
I left your key in the dish by the door
Like a tooth for a fairy who don't come anymore
Each morning I check what the night might have paid
It's still just the key, and the bed that I made
I'd love to hear your thoughts.

I'm 19, make lo-fi bedroom pop, and this is the hook of my next upload:
One percent, still lit
Ten tabs open, can't commit
Everybody asks how I am
I say "charging" and I mean it
Let me know what you think, no pressure lol

I've fixed cars for twenty years and play bluegrass banjo on weekends. I wrote this chorus for the band:
Take the Cadillac, take the county line
Take the gold in the ground and the mine
Leave me a porch with two chairs and you
And a hound that don't care what I do
What's your honest reaction?

I'm a taxi driver, 40, and I moved here eleven years ago. I've been turning my feelings into songs. This is the chorus of the newest:
I wear two watches, one for here, one for home
One says it's noon, one says you're asleep
I live in the hours that don't have a name
Keeping time for the ones I can't keep
I'd be grateful for your opinion.

I'm 71 and I direct my church choir. I wrote a Christmas song for us this year, and this is the chorus:
Hang the crooked star on the crooked tree
It's leaned that way since sixty-three
Nothing we love ever stood up straight
It just stayed standing, and so did we
Would you tell me how it strikes you?

I'm a software engineer writing synth-pop on the side, and I wrote this about my husband and me fighting over the thermostat. Chorus:
You want sixty-eight, I want seventy-two
So we live at seventy and both of us are wrong
Ten years of compromise in a little glowing number
That's the temperature of home
Any feedback is welcome!

I wrote this chorus for my nana after she passed in March. I'm a sophomore and have never shared a song before, so my hands are a little shaky. Does it work for you?
You measured flour in the hollow of your palm,
salt by the weather, sugar by your mood.
Now I'm guessing in your chipped blue bowl,
and the bread comes out almost you,
and almost is a kind of company, too.

Hey! I own a small bakery and wrote a song on my 4 a.m. shifts. Here's the chorus. Would love to hear what you make of it, honestly.
Four a.m., the oven's breathing, the whole street's still in bed,
I'm the only one who knows the sun is made of bread.
Flour on my eyelashes, the radio turned low,
somebody's gonna wake up warm to something I made slow.

I drive long-haul and write country songs on my breaks, mostly for fun. This is the chorus of my newest one. Tell me what you think, don't hold back.
Every porch light on I-80 is a small yellow you,
I count them like rosary beads till the sun comes through.
None of them are mine, but I tip my hat to every one that's burning:
somebody's waiting up, and by sunrise one is mine.

I'm a college junior and this is the chorus of a song for my environmental studies capstone, which for some reason let me submit music. Can you tell me how it reads?
We planted a tree the year the ice went thin,
my dad says it'll shade my kids if they begin.
So I water it like an argument I'm winning slow.
Roots don't read the news, they just know where to go.

I run a tiny flower shop and write songs at the counter between orders. This chorus came out of a really long Valentine's week. I'd love an outside opinion!
Nobody buys peonies when everything's fine,
it's funerals, apologies, "please be mine."
I wrap the worst days in brown paper and twine
and send them out smelling like maybe in time.

First-gen student here. I wrote this hook after an internship interview and I'm kind of nervous to show anyone. What's your honest take?
Mama dusted the boardroom where I'm interviewing now,
she knew the table's every scar and never knew how
to ask for a seat there. So I'll sit, and I'll stay,
with her name in my mouth like the first thing I say.

I commute by ferry every day and started writing a shanty about it, just for my own amusement. Here's the chorus. Tell me what you think, mates!
Oh, the 7:15's a whale with a belly full of us,
coffee-breathed and sleepy, swallowed without fuss.
Spit us out at Pier Nine, we'll scatter like the gulls,
and at six she'll swallow us again, and we'll be glad, we'll be glad.

Astronomy major, and I also write songs in the stairwell of my dorm. This is the chorus of one I finished last night. Curious how it lands for someone hearing it cold.
That star might've died a thousand years ago,
and still it's reaching us. We'll never know.
So if you leave, leave the way starlight leaves:
keep arriving, keep arriving, long after you were.

I keep bees on my roof and have been writing a lullaby for them, which sounds silly out loud. Here's the chorus. Would you mind telling me what you think?
Forty thousand sisters and none of them asks why,
they carry out the winter and they carry in July.
I've been trying to learn how a thing so small
can work like it's the only one and still be one of all.

I'm a nursing student doing overnights, and this chorus showed up around 3 a.m. last week. I'm posting it here to get another set of eyes. Thoughts?
At three a.m. the hallway hums like a held breath,
a hundred sleeping strangers and my shoes the only sound.
I check that each one's breathing, it's the whole job, nothing less,
and I walk the dark like love with a clipboard, going round.

I own a laundromat, and my customers inspired a song, so here's the chorus. English is my second language, so I'm curious how the words sound to you. What do you think?
Spin cycle, spin cycle, the whole block's laundry turning,
I learned my English at the folding tables here.
Every lonely sock, I keep in a box by the door.
Someone always comes back, if you wait a year.

Just finished this chorus and I'm kind of buzzing, so I'm sharing it right away. I'm a senior in high school, and it's about my town. Tell me what you think!
Everybody here knows my middle name and my mother's,
the truck my dad sold, the fence I drove through.
I'm leaving in June with one bag and no one's blessing.
God, I hope someplace else knows me half as well as you.

I'm a retired teacher who took up guitar last year. This chorus is about my last day in the classroom. I'd appreciate any feedback you're willing to give.
Thirty-one Septembers of a room that smelled of chalk,
I learned a thousand names and then I watched them walk.
They'll forget the dates and the dull parts I taught,
but they'll remember who was glad they came, and that's a lot.

I teach pottery classes out of my small studio and wrote this at the wheel, then recorded a voice memo. Here's the chorus. Does it come across the way I hope?
The clay remembers every time you flinched,
a thumbprint in the foot of every cup.
Fire it hot enough and it won't mind.
It'll call the shaking part of what holds up.

ok so this is the chorus to a breakup song I wrote in my dorm and my roommate just laughed at me, which wasn't helpful lol. Can I get a real opinion?
I deleted your number but my thumbs know the way,
they dial you in the dark like they've got something to say.
My head's moved out, my head's got a new address,
but my thumbs are still squatting in the mess.

I've run a small auto repair shop for twenty years and just started writing blues in the back office. Here's a chorus I've been humming all week. What do you reckon?
She's got two hundred thousand miles and a rattle in her chest,
but she turns over first try in the cold, and that's the test.
Don't tell me she's worn out, she's just finally honest.
Every sound she makes is true, and I'm the only one who's listening.

I'm 19 and wrote this for my little brother. I've never played it for anyone, and I'm a bit nervous posting it. How does it read to you?
You're nine and you think I know everything,
I'm nineteen and bluffing with a straight face.
So I'll keep standing like a lighthouse, kid,
till you're old enough to see I'm a light on a rock, scared of the waves too.

I own a neighborhood bar and wrote a singalong for our regulars. This is the chorus, written after we lost one of them. Wondering what you'd say about it.
Raise one to the ones who closed the place with us,
and one to the stool by the door that's empty now.
We keep the light on, Tommy, we don't make a fuss.
You'll always have a tab here, we just never wrote it down.

Weekend gardener here, and my zucchini has gotten completely out of hand. I turned it into a country chorus. Be straight with me, what's your take?
Zucchini in July, please, I'm begging you stop,
I've left bags on porches, I've filled the church shop.
The neighbors all wave with a too-careful smile.
They've seen me coming up the drive for a mile.

I'm training for my first marathon and wrote a song on my long runs. Here's the chorus! I'd love to hear how it comes across to someone who hasn't heard it before.
Mile twenty is where the liars quit,
my legs file complaints, my lungs pick sides.
But past the wall there's a quiet that fits,
and the only one waiting there is me, arriving.

New dad, and I've been writing at 3 a.m. while pacing the hallway. This is the chorus so far. I'd really like a second opinion if you have a minute.
It's three a.m. and you're the smallest alarm clock,
set by nothing but wanting to be near.
I'll be the tired thing that comes when you call.
There are worse jobs than being who you want here.

I run a used bookshop and wrote a jazzy little number about it. Here's the chorus. I'd be curious about your reaction, whatever it is.
Every book on this shelf was somebody's Tuesday night,
a train ride, a bathtub, a borrowed flashlight.
I just keep the kettle on and the lamp lit low,
and the dead keep writing to whoever's up.

I drive a food truck and wrote this on a napkin during a slow Tuesday, then turned it into a chorus. Please tell me what you think of it!
Tacos at midnight, the line wraps the block,
a nurse, a bouncer, a guy off the clock.
Everybody's tired, nobody's fine,
but for ninety seconds, we're all kind.

I'm a music-minded cashier at a hardware store, and I wrote this chorus about the guy who comes in every Saturday for one screw. I'd like to know what you think.
He buys one screw and he stays an hour,
talks about the weather, talks about the flour
of his late wife's biscuits, and the shelf he never built.
I ring him up slow. Some things aren't meant to be fixed.

I'm a grad student who writes songs to cope with deadlines. This chorus is about my grandfather's radio, which I still keep on my desk. Does it work as a chorus, in your view?
He tuned it by feel, a quarter inch of static,
found the ballgame in the hiss like a man finding a door.
Now it sits on my desk, picking up nothing,
but I turn the dial anyway. I just want to hear it once more.

Starting my Etsy candle shop resume! Bullet: "Founded and CEO of multinational candle corporation with global operations, operating out of my bedroom." Curious what you'd say about it.

Nervous about this! I tutored math in high school and wrote: "Tutored students in math, such as algebra, geometry, calculus, and the subject of mathematics generally, improving their grades." Thoughts?

I'm so excited to send this out. For my food truck: "Increased tacos sales by 3,000% in one week, from 2 tacos to 62, while being ranked the number one truck in the world." Can you tell me your thoughts?

Just graduated and applying for backend jobs. This is the first bullet under my internship: "Reduced p95 checkout API latency from 1.8s to 310ms by replacing N+1 Postgres queries with batched lookups and adding a read-through Redis cache, saving an estimated $42K/yr in compute." I've never run before but I signed up for a marathon in 3 weeks. Here's my training: Mon: 10 miles. Tue: 12 miles. Wed: 14 miles. Thu: 16 miles. Fri: 18 miles. Sat: 20 miles. Sun: 22 miles. I'm 38 and work in sales. What do you think?

I'm a high school teacher and here's my weekly workout plan. Monday: gym. Tuesday: gym. Wednesday: gym. Thursday: gym. Friday: gym. Saturday: gym. Sunday: gym. I'll just do whatever machines are free. Any thoughts on it?

I'm 55 with two bad knees but I want to get serious. Mon: heavy squats and box jumps. Tue: lunges and stair sprints. Wed: jump rope 30 min. Thu: deep squats again. Fri: plyometrics. Sat: hill running. Sun: rest. What's your take?

Been lifting for a year and I'm 22, working as a cashier. My plan: Mon: biceps and chest. Tue: shoulders and biceps. Wed: chest. Thu: biceps. Fri: chest and shoulders. Sat: biceps. Sun: rest. I skip legs because nobody sees them anyway. Can you review it?

I'm 41 and want to build muscle. Plan is 30 minutes on the treadmill every day, Monday through Sunday, at the same speed. No weights because they make me bulky. I'll add 5 minutes next year. What do you think? Be gentle, I'm a bit shy about this.

Accountant here, I like precision, so here's my Monday: 6:00 stretch, 6:01 pushups, 6:03 water, 6:04 squats, 6:06 water, 6:07 lunges, 6:09 pushups, 6:10 stretch. Tuesday through Sunday are the same. I know it's long, but how does it look?

I started yoga two weeks ago and put together this routine! Mon: 1 hr handstand practice. Tue: 1 hr handstand. Wed: full splits for 90 min. Thu: handstand. Fri: handstand and splits. Sat: rest. Sun: handstand. I'm 27 and a graphic designer. Thoughts?

I'm a busy lawyer so I made it efficient. Mon, Wed, Fri: one 3-hour session with chest, back, legs, arms, shoulders, abs, and cardio, all to failure. Tue, Thu, Sat, Sun: nothing, since I'll be sore. Could you let me know what you think?

Dad of three, 40, trying to get strong. Every day I do bench press, 5 sets of 20 at my max weight. Monday to Saturday. Sunday I do bench press too, but lighter. That's it, since bench is the best exercise. What's your opinion of my plan?

I'm a 33-year-old swimmer, and this is my week. Mon: swim 5 km. Tue: swim 5 km. Wed: swim 5 km. Thu: swim 5 km. Fri: swim 5 km. Sat: swim 5 km. Sun: run a marathon for cross-training. I don't lift. Wondering what you'd say.

Retired army guy, 60. My plan is simple. Mon-Sat: 5 am, no warmup, max effort until failure, and push through any pain, since pain is weakness leaving the body. Sunday I rest if I can. I don't track anything. Any feedback for me?

I'm a 20-year-old student with a tight schedule. Every day I eat a huge lunch at 12:30 and start a 1-hour HIIT workout at 12:45 so I don't waste time. Fridays I add a second HIIT in the evening. Please tell me what you think of it.

so my plan is basically that on monday I do some arms and then maybe legs but legs is also tuesday and then cardio is whenever, wednesday is rest unless I did cardio, thursday is arms again and friday I do the full body or abs and sat is Sunday's thing. I'm 31, chef. what do u think?

I'm 15 and I want visible abs ASAP. Plan: 1000 situps every day, Monday to Sunday, 500 in the morning and 500 before bed. I don't do anything else since situps are the only thing that works for abs. Could you share your opinion?

Hi! I'm a 26-year-old paralegal, and I made a leg day for Wednesday: bicep curls, tricep dips, shoulder press, lateral raises, and chest flies. Other days are similar, with Thursday being back day, which is all calf raises. Rest is on Sunday. Can you tell me what you think?

Hi! I'm a college sophomore and I made my first workout plan to get ripped by spring break (6 weeks). Mon: chest, Tue: chest and arms, Wed: arms, Thu: chest, Fri: arms and chest, Sat: chest, Sun: chest if I have energy. 100 pushups each day too. Can you tell me what you think?

Here's my weekly plan, I'm trying to lose 20 lbs in two weeks for a wedding:
Mon–Sun: run 10 miles, 500 calorie diet, 300 situps, 1 hour HIIT.
I've never really exercised before but I'm super motivated. Thoughts?

I run a small home-based personal training business and I wrote this for a client: Monday: cardio. Tuesday: weights. Wednesday: cardio. Thursday: weights. Friday: cardio and weights. Saturday: stretching. Sunday: rest. I'll put it in my welcome packet. Any feedback before I send it out?

so this is my weekly workout lol. Mon legs, Tue legs, Wed skip leg day, Thu upper body, Fri rest, Sat legs, Sun rest. I only do squats tho cuz they work everything. Kinda proud of it ngl. what do u think?

I'm a high school student trying out for the soccer team. My plan: Monday, run until I throw up. Tuesday, run until I throw up. Wednesday, rest (drink only water). Thursday, run until I throw up. Friday, scrimmage. Weekend: run more. Could you give me your opinion?

I'm nervous to share this, but here's my first plan as a beginner: Monday: exercise. Tuesday: exercise a little. Wednesday: exercise some more. Thursday: rest or exercise. Friday: exercise. Saturday: exercise hard. Sunday: relax. Is this a good structure to follow?

I own a tiny yoga studio and I'm posting this 'Weekly Wellness Plan' on our wall: Mon – yoga. Tue – yoga. Wed – yoga with a different pose. Thu – more yoga. Fri – yoga flow. Sat – yoga and meditation. Sun – recovery yoga. Would you change anything?

Here's my gym schedule! Mon: bench press 10 sets of 20 reps, Tue: squats 10 sets of 20 reps, Wed: deadlifts 10 sets of 20 reps, Thu: all three again, Fri: max out on everything, Sat: max out again. I eat only salad. Let me know what you think!

I'm a nursing student with no time, so I made this plan: Monday 5am gym 2 hrs, Tuesday 5am gym 2 hrs, Wednesday 5am gym 2 hrs, Thursday 5am gym 2 hrs, Friday 5am gym 2 hrs. I usually sleep around 3 hours on clinical nights. Can you review it for me?

Hey, I'm a hobby cyclist and I wrote this week for myself: Mon: bike 20 miles. Tue: bike 20 miles. Wed: bike 20 miles. Thu: bike 20 miles. Fri: bike 20 miles. Sat: bike 20 miles. Sun: bike 20 miles. I want to improve my running time for a 5K. Thoughts?

I'm 58 and starting out again after years off, and I made this plan for myself: Mon: 5-mile sprint intervals, Tue: heavy deadlifts, Wed: box jumps, Thu: another 5-mile sprint session, Fri: max-weight bench, Sat: marathon-distance run, Sun: rest. I'd love your opinion.

Dear reader, I created a plan for my bakery staff's wellness challenge. Monday: be active. Tuesday: be active in a different way. Wednesday: drink water and be active. Thursday: be active with a coworker. Friday: celebrate with a donut. Saturday and Sunday: stay active. Does this seem okay to hand out?

Here's my weekly routine for building huge biceps: Monday: curls. Tuesday: curls. Wednesday: hammer curls. Thursday: curls with a different grip. Friday: curls. Saturday: preacher curls. Sunday: rest from curls. I'm a college freshman and I'm pumped to start. Any feedback?

I'm a grad student and I made a plan around my study schedule: Mon 6am run, Tue 6am run, Wed no workout because exams, Thu no workout, Fri no workout, Sat no workout, Sun big 4-hour workout to make up for everything. What do you think?

As a small CrossFit box owner, I drafted our member week: Mon: 100 burpees, 100 pull-ups, 100 squats. Tue: same. Wed: same, but faster. Thu: same with a weighted vest. Fri: 200 of each. Sat: 300 of each. Sun: recover. Beginners welcome! How does it look?

My weekly plan to lose belly fat: Mon: 500 crunches. Tue: 500 crunches. Wed: 600 crunches. Thu: 600 crunches. Fri: 700 crunches. Sat: 700 crunches. Sun: rest, since spot-reduction takes a break too. I read it online somewhere. Thoughts please?

Quick question! I'm in 8th grade and made this plan: Mon: jog 1 min. Tue: jog 1 min. Wed: jog 1 min and stretch 1 min. Thu: jog 1 min. Fri: jog 1 min. Sat: pizza. Sun: nap. I want to be an Olympic sprinter by next summer. What do you think?

I'm a yoga hobbyist and put together this plan: Monday: Headstand for 45 minutes. Tuesday: Headstand for 45 minutes plus handstands. Wednesday: Wheel pose 30 minutes. Thursday: Headstand again. Friday: advanced arm balances. No warmup, since I'm flexible already. Can I get your opinion?

I run a small online fitness coaching business and this is my '7-Day Shred' program: Day 1: Cardio. Day 2: Strength. Day 3: Cardio. Day 4: Strength. Day 5: Cardio. Day 6: Strength. Day 7: Cardio. Guaranteed to burn 10 lbs of fat in a week! I'm about to put it on my website. Thoughts?

Hi everyone, I'm a hobbyist weightlifter and here's my plan: Mon – Back. Tue – Biceps. Wed – Back. Thu – Back and biceps. Fri – Biceps. Sat – Back. Sun – Back. I don't train chest, legs, or shoulders since no one sees them. Could you let me know what you think?

I'm a part-time barista and a busy mom, so here's my plan: Monday: wake up and exercise for however long. Tuesday: exercise when the kids nap, if they nap. Wednesday: try to exercise. Thursday: exercise. Friday: exercise at some point. Weekend: see how I feel. Does that sound okay to you?

Here's the swim plan I wrote for my first triathlon in 3 weeks: Mon: swim 5 miles. Tue: swim 5 miles. Wed: swim 5 miles. Thu: swim 5 miles. Fri: swim 5 miles. Sat: swim 5 miles. I'll skip bike and run, since swimming is the hardest anyway. Can you give me feedback?

I'm a senior in high school and wrote my plan for the wrestling season! Mon: sauna 3 hrs to cut weight, Tue: sauna 3 hrs and run in a garbage bag, Wed: no water, Thu: practice, Fri: match. Sat/Sun: eat everything. Pretty excited about it. What's your opinion?

I own a small hiking tour company and drafted a training week for our guides: Monday: walk. Tuesday: walk further. Wednesday: walk uphill. Thursday: walk with a backpack. Friday: walk uphill with a backpack. Saturday: long walk. Sunday: walk to recover. I'd like your feedback, please!

My workout plan: Monday, Wednesday, and Friday I do 3 hours of cardio, plus 3 hours of weights, plus 2 hours of stretching, then I go to work 9 to 5 and study for my night classes until 1am. Tuesday and Thursday are the same but longer. Weekends I rest and plan. How does it look?

I'm an ER nurse on rotating 12-hour shifts, so I built my week around shifts instead of weekdays. Shift day: 10 minutes of hip and thoracic mobility only. Day after a shift: 5x5 trap-bar deadlift, 3x8 split squats. Second day off: upper body, four push/pull supersets. Third day off: 40-minute zone-2 run. After three nights in a row, I swap the heavy day for an easy 30-minute bike. What's your honest opinion?

I'm 16, a goalkeeper, and season starts in six weeks. Mon: box jumps 4x4, band-resisted lateral shuffles. Tue: team practice. Wed: pull-ups 4x6, Nordic curls 3x5, Copenhagen planks. Thu: practice, then 10 minutes of tennis-ball reaction catches off a wall. Fri: mobility only. Sat: match. Sun: easy swim, shoulder prehab. Nothing heavy within 48 hours of a match, so I planned around that. Any thoughts? Be straight with me.

I'm 71 and my doctor mentioned osteopenia. Mon/Thu: 50 heel drops, step-ups in a 5 kg weighted vest, farmer carries with 8 kg. Tue/Sat: 45-minute brisk hill walk. Wed: tai chi class, plus one-minute single-leg stands while brushing my teeth. Fri: band rows, wall push-ups moving toward counter push-ups. Sun: gardening. I add 1 kg to the vest each month. I'd love to hear what you make of it.

I'm a 29-year-old climber working toward my first 8a. Mon: 4 max hangs on a 20mm edge (10 s, +5 kg), then limit bouldering. Tue: 40-minute zone-2 bike, core. Wed: rest. Thu: 4x4s on routes two grades below my limit. Fri: push-ups, reverse wrist curls, shoulder external rotation. Sat: project attempts while fresh. Sun: rest. Every fourth week I halve the volume. How does it look to you?

First-time dad here, and baby's naps are unpredictable, so everything is 12 minutes with zero setup. Mon/Wed/Fri: EMOM, odd minutes 8 push-ups, even minutes 10 squats holding a 12 kg backpack. Tue/Thu: stroller walk, 1 minute fast, 2 easy, five rounds. Sat: Monday's session plus a 2-minute plank. Sun: rest. Honestly I'm a bit nervous sharing this. What do you think?

Week 10 of my marathon block, aiming for 3:15. Mon: rest, 15 minutes of yoga. Tue: 8x400 m at 5k pace, 90 s jog. Wed: 10 km easy plus 6 strides. Thu: 16 km with 8 km at marathon pace (4:37/km). Fri: rest. Sat: 8 km easy, then 30 minutes of single-leg RDLs and calf raises. Sun: 30 km, last 5 at goal pace. About 85 km total. Would you change anything?

I'm 26, entering my first powerlifting meet in 12 weeks (63 kg class). Mon: heavy squat triples at RPE 8, paused bench 4x5. Wed: 3x3 deadlifts off 2-inch blocks, overhead press, rows. Fri: bench single then 3x6 backoffs, paused squats 5x3 at 75%. Tue/Thu: 20 minutes of easy bike, face pulls, abs. Weekends off. Deload in week 9, then a two-week peak. Feedback welcome!

I'm 40 and a T10 paraplegic. I want to build strength without wrecking my shoulders. Mon: seated cable rows 4x10, face pulls 3x15, landmine press 3x8. Tue: handcycle intervals, 6x2 min hard/2 easy. Wed: rest. Thu: lat pulldowns 4x8, parallel-bar dips 3x6, rotator cuff band work. Fri: 30-minute steady handcycle. Sat: Pallof presses and core. Sun: rest. Pulling volume is double pushing on purpose. Thoughts?

I'm 22 weeks pregnant and my midwife cleared me to exercise. Mon: 30-minute incline walk, goblet squats to a box 3x10, side-lying clamshells. Tue: prenatal yoga video. Wed: 25-minute swim. Thu: dumbbell rows, seated shoulder press, five minutes of pelvic floor breathing. Fri: rest. Sat: long walk with my sister. Sun: stretching. Nothing flat on my back, nothing above RPE 6. I'd love to hear what you think.

Casual question: I'm 45, sit at a desk nine hours a day, and my shoulders are creeping forward. Mon/Thu: rows, face pulls, wall angels, dead bugs. Tue/Fri: hip flexor stretch, glute bridges, goblet squats, 20-minute walk. Wed: swim or bike, whatever. Weekend: one hike. Plus a 2-minute doorway chest stretch every time my coffee finishes. Does this make sense? Roast me if needed.

I'm a 31-year-old firefighter preparing for our annual physical agility test. Mon: stair climbs in a 20 kg vest, 5x3 minutes. Tue: sled drags 6x20 m, farmer carries 4x40 m. Wed: 40-minute easy run. Thu: cable hose-pull simulation 5x30 s, dummy drags. Fri: heavy deadlifts 5x3. Sat: full timed test circuit. Sun: rest, foam roll. Does this seem right to you?

I'm a 52-year-old masters swimmer and the 200 free is my race. Mon: 3000 m, 10x100 on 1:30. Tue: dryland with band pulls and medicine-ball rotations. Wed: 2500 m, 8x50 all-out with 30 s rest. Thu: off. Fri: 3200 m, 4x200 descending. Sat: 2000 m technique, catch-up and fist drills, 20 minutes of core. Sun: rest. I'm curious what a coach would say.

I'm a 24-year-old ballet dancer, rehearsing six days a week, so cross-training can't add leg fatigue. Mon: 10 minutes of pre-class glute band work. Tue: Pilates reformer. Wed: upper body only, push-ups and rows, 3x10. Thu: slow single-leg calf raises 3x15, tibialis raises. Fri: nothing. Sat: 20 minutes of easy bike. Sun: complete rest, no stretching. Would you change anything?

Broke college student, dorm room, no equipment. Mon/Thu: push-up progression (incline, regular, archer) for 5 rounds, towel rows around a door frame. Tue/Fri: Bulgarian split squats off my bed 4x10 each side, single-leg glute bridges. Wed: 25-minute run around campus. Sat: 10 minutes of wall handstand practice. Sun: rest. I log reps and add one rep a week. Rate it however you like!

I farm 120 acres, and at 50, harvest wipes me out. So this is my harvest-season week: Mon/Wed/Fri, 15 minutes before breakfast. Kettlebell hinges (20 kg) 3x10, suitcase carries 3x40 m, dead hangs 3x30 s, doorway chest opener. Tue/Thu: 20-minute walk along the field edge. Sat/Sun: nothing. Everything counters what the tractor and bales do to my hips, grip and shoulders. What do you think?

I'm 63, diagnosed with Parkinson's two years ago. My neurologist said big, fast and frequent. Mon/Wed/Fri: 20 minutes of LSVT BIG-style movements, then boxing on a heavy bag, 6x2 minutes. Tue/Thu: 30-minute cycling class at 80+ rpm. Sat: dance class. Sun: voice exercises and a walk with poles. I do the hardest sessions when my meds peak. Could you give me your opinion?

I'm a 28-year-old BJJ blue belt. Mon/Wed/Fri: class and rolling. Tue: towel pull-ups 4x5, farmer holds 3x45 s, neck bridges 2x20. Thu: assault bike sprints, 8x20 s on/40 s off, then hip mobility. Sat: one hour of drilling with a partner. Sun: rest. No lifting before I roll. Any feedback on how this fits together?

I'm 55, a veteran, with chronic lower back pain. Every morning, 10 minutes: McGill big three (curl-up, side plank, bird dog), 10-second holds. Mon/Thu: dowel hip-hinge practice, then light trap-bar deadlifts 3x8. Tue/Sat: 30-minute walk. Wed: dead hangs, cat-cow. Fri: pool. Sun: rest. I only progress when next-morning pain is under 3 out of 10. What do you think?

Mom of three, so my workouts ride on existing routines. Mon: while the pasta boils, 3 rounds of 10 squats and 10 counter push-ups. Tue: school-run walk, pushing the stroller up the big hill. Wed: during swim lessons, 30 laps. Thu: 20-minute kettlebell video while the kids watch a show. Fri: 15-minute kitchen dance party. Sat: family hike carrying the youngest. Sun: rest. Does this seem sustainable?

I'm a 47-year-old long-haul trucker, on the road five days a week. I keep bands and a suspension trainer in the cab. Mon-Fri at every fuel stop: 5 minutes of band pull-aparts and hip circles. Evenings, 20 minutes alternating A/B. A: suspension rows, split squats. B: push-ups, single-leg RDLs. Sat: 5 km walk at home. Sun: rest. Wondering how this reads to you.

I have ADHD and get bored by week two, so my plan has fixed anchors and random variety. Mon legs, Tue push, Thu pull, Sat carries and run. Each day's main lift never changes (squat, press, row, farmer carry). Accessories come from rolling a die against a list of six per day. Wed/Fri: 20-minute walk with podcasts. Sun: off. Tracking is one tick on the fridge. Do you think it holds together?

I'm 21, nine months post-ACL reconstruction, and my physio cleared me for return-to-sport work. Mon: single-leg press 4x8 with a 3-second lower, Nordics 3x5. Tue: low box jumps with stuck landings 4x5, deceleration drills. Thu: heavy RDLs, hip thrusts. Fri: straight-line runs 6x60 m at 80%. Sat: pool. Wed/Sun: off. Hop tests are next month, so I'm tracking limb symmetry. Feedback?

I'm 33, a software engineer, with a 50 km mountain race in October, and I live somewhere flat. Mon: 1 hour treadmill at 12% incline. Tue: eccentric step-ups with a 10 kg pack, 5x12 per leg. Wed: 8 km easy. Thu: parking-garage stair repeats, 6x10 floors. Fri: rest. Sat: 3-hour trail run, eating every 30 minutes as practice. Sun: 60-minute poles hike. Thoughts?

I'm 68 and want my clubhead speed back. Mon/Thu: cable chops, 3 kg medicine-ball rotational throws against a wall 3x8, goblet squats. Tue/Fri: walk 5 km, carrying my bag. Wed: 20 minutes of hip and thoracic mobility. Sat: golf. Sun: rest. I'm tracking my driver speed on the range once a month. Does this look reasonable to you?

I'm 40 and have never lifted before, so I kept it simple. Mon/Wed/Fri: goblet squat, dumbbell bench, one-arm row, Romanian deadlift, plank, always in that order. Start at 3x8, add one rep per week until 3x12, then add weight. Tue/Thu: 20-minute walk. Sat: something fun. Sun: rest. I write down how I felt after each session. I'm a bit nervous about sharing it. What do you think?

Hi! I'm a sophomore rower and built this off-season week around my 2k erg test in March. Mon: 60 min UT2 at 18-20spm. Tue: squats 5x5, rows 4x6, core. Wed: 8x500m at 2k pace, 2:00 rest. Thu: mobility only. Fri: deadlifts 4x4, 45 min UT2. Sat: 90 min steady. Sun: off. I put heavy lifting the day before easy rows so the hard erg day stays fresh. What do you think?

I run a small bakery and I'm up at 3:30am, so my plan bends around that. Mon/Thu: 25 min kettlebell circuit at 2pm (swings, goblet squats, rows). Tue/Fri: 30 min walk plus hip and thoracic mobility for my flour-bag back. Wed: full rest, nap included. Sat: easy 45 min bike with my daughter. Sun: closed, so a long hike. Honest thoughts? Anything you'd tweak?

Climbing hobbyist here, three years in, with a pulley tweak last spring. Mon: hangboard 4x10s on 20mm, half-crimp, bodyweight minus 10kg, then push-ups. Tue: easy volume on V2-V3, 60 min. Wed: rest. Thu: limit bouldering, long rests, stop when quality drops. Fri: rest and shoulder band work. Sat: outdoors. Sun: 30 min yoga. Would love your opinion on how it's laid out.

I'm 16 and trying to get ready for soccer preseason in August. Mon: sprints 6x30m, walk-back recovery, then Nordic curls 3x5. Tue: lower-body lift plus core. Wed: 40 min easy jog or ball work. Thu: agility ladder, cone cuts, single-leg hops. Fri: upper body plus mobility. Sat: pickup game. Sun: rest. I'm a bit nervous showing this to anyone. Could you give me feedback?

I own a flower shop and I'm training for my first marathon (week 10 of 16). Mon: rest. Tue: 8 miles easy. Wed: 6 miles with 3x1 mile at tempo. Thu: 5 easy plus strides, 20 min strength. Fri: rest. Sat: 16 mile long run, last 3 at goal pace. Sun: 4 recovery miles. Wedding season hits in May, so Fridays stay empty on purpose. What's your take?

I'm 24 weeks pregnant and my OB cleared me for exercise. Mon: 30 min prenatal yoga. Tue: incline walk 35 min at conversational pace. Wed: goblet squats, band rows, side-lying glute work, 3 sets each. Thu: rest. Fri: swim 30 min. Sat: pelvic floor and breathing work plus a short walk. Sun: rest. Anything you'd adjust or add, in your opinion? Thanks so much!

I'm 68 and retired, and my main goal is staying steady on my feet for gardening and grandkids. Mon: 20 min walk, sit-to-stand 3x10, heel-to-toe walking. Tue: resistance bands, upper body. Wed: tai chi class. Thu: walk plus single-leg stands near the counter. Fri: light dumbbell work. Sat: garden (counts!). Sun: rest. Does this seem like a reasonable week to you?

I use a manual wheelchair and wanted a plan that protects my shoulders. Mon: pull-focused day: band pull-aparts, seated cable rows, face pulls. Tue: 30 min hand-cycle intervals, 1 min hard/2 easy. Wed: core and scapular stability. Thu: rest. Fri: press day, kept lighter than pulls at a 2:1 ratio. Sat: 45 min easy push outdoors. Sun: stretching. Can you tell me what you think of the balance?

Powerlifting hobbyist, meet is in 8 days. Mon: squat 3x2 at 85%, bench 3x3 at 80%. Tue: rest. Wed: deadlift 2x2 at 85%, easy accessory work. Thu: bench singles up to 90%, short walk. Fri: rest. Sat: openers only, 30 min mobility. Sun: travel, light food, sleep. Volume drops about 40% while intensity stays high. Would love a second pair of eyes on this taper.

I'm a dance major with auditions in six weeks and a history of tight hips. Mon: ballet technique, then 20 min glute and hip strengthening. Tue: Pilates reformer. Wed: jump training, 3x8 box jumps plus calf raises. Thu: contemporary class, then foam rolling. Fri: stamina, 3 run-throughs of my audition piece. Sat: swim, easy. Sun: off. How would you rate the structure of my week?

I teach yoga part-time and run a tiny studio, and I keep forgetting to train myself. So: Mon/Wed/Fri 20 min lifts before my first class (deadlift, press, pull-ups, one lift each, 4 sets). Tue/Thu: I teach, that's my cardio. Sat: trail run with a friend. Sun: restorative practice, no phone. Short on purpose so I actually do it. What do you make of it?

Parkour beginner, four months in. Mon: wrist and ankle prep, 30 min of precision jumps and quadrupedal movement. Tue: pull-ups 5x5, dips 4x8, hanging leg raises. Wed: rest. Thu: vault and roll practice at low heights, 45 min. Fri: squats and single-leg work. Sat: jam at the park with my crew. Sun: mobility. I keep progressions small to avoid joint issues. Thoughts, anyone?

Grad student with exactly three hours a week to spare. Mon, Wed, Fri: 45 min full-body strength, A/B/A then B/A/B. A: squat, bench, row. B: deadlift, overhead press, pull-ups. Each lift is 3 sets, adding 2.5kg whenever all reps are clean. Tue and Thu: 10-minute walk after lunch for thesis-brain fog. Weekends are completely free of training. Do you have any feedback on it?

Masters swimmer here, age 41, training for a 1500m open water race. Mon: 3000m, drills plus 10x100 on 1:40. Tue: dryland, band pulls, core. Wed: 5x400 steady at race pace. Thu: rest. Fri: 2500m with sighting practice every 8th stroke. Sat: open-water swim, 40 min. Sun: rest. How does this look to you? I'm not sure about two quality swims on consecutive days.

I'm a cyclist chasing a higher FTP before a gran fondo. Mon: rest. Tue: 3x12 min at 95% FTP, 6 min between. Wed: 60 min Zone 2. Thu: 5x4 min VO2 efforts, 4 min rest. Fri: rest or spin. Sat: 3 hr endurance with fueling practice every 30 min. Sun: 90 min easy. Hard days are kept apart by easy days so I keep my legs fresh. Could you give me your thoughts?

I run a food truck and spend 10 hours a day on concrete, bending and lifting. My week: Mon/Wed: 30 min of calf, hip and lower-back strength (split squats, hip thrusts, bird dogs). Tue/Thu: swim or walk, whatever my feet allow. Fri: rest before the weekend rush. Sat/Sun: 5 minutes of stretches before each service. Nothing heavy because the job already is. What are your thoughts?

Small apartment, one pair of 20kg adjustable dumbbells, no complaints. Mon: goblet squats, floor press, one-arm rows, 4 sets of 8 with a 3-second lowering phase. Tue: 20 min brisk walk. Wed: Romanian deadlifts, split squats, pushups, 4x10. Thu: rest. Fri: repeat Monday but add a pause rep. Sat: long walk. Sun: rest. I progress by tempo before weight. Does that make sense to you?

I'm hiking Kilimanjaro in September and have 12 weeks. Mon: stair climb with a 10kg pack, 45 min. Tue: strength (step-ups, lunges, calf raises). Wed: rest. Thu: 5 miles easy with a pack. Fri: yoga for hips and breathing practice. Sat: 4-6 hour hike with elevation gain, adding an hour every two weeks. Sun: 40 min easy walk. I'll swap in a sauna session twice weekly for heat. Opinions welcome!

Club tennis player with a cranky right shoulder. Mon: serve practice, 40 balls, then rotator-cuff external rotations. Tue: legs and lateral lunges. Wed: match play, 90 min. Thu: rest and thoracic mobility. Fri: med-ball rotational throws, 4x6 each side. Sat: drills and footwork. Sun: off. I keep serve volume capped so the shoulder gets recovery. Could you tell me how this reads to you?

Six months post ACL reconstruction. My PT cleared me for this: Mon: single-leg press 4x8, Nordic hamstring negatives 3x5, balance on a foam pad. Tue: stationary bike 30 min. Wed: step-downs, hip bridges, calf raises. Thu: rest. Fri: light jogging intervals, 1 min on/2 min walk x8. Sat: swim. Sun: rest. I track knee swelling after each session. I'd appreciate your thoughts, I'm kind of anxious about it.

I'm a barista, so my feet are tired, but I walk my greyhound every morning anyway. Mon: dog walk plus 20 min bodyweight (squats, pushups, planks). Tue: dog walk, shift. Wed: dog walk plus 20 min band work. Thu: shift, then rest. Fri: dog walk plus bodyweight circuit. Sat: long 90 min walk with the dog in the park. Sun: sleeping in. What would you change, if anything?

Calisthenics hobbyist working toward my first muscle-up. Mon: weighted pull-ups 5x3, explosive pull-ups 4x4, false grip hangs. Tue: dips 4x8, pike push-ups, hollow holds. Wed: rest. Thu: transition drills with a band, 6x3, and straight-bar dips. Fri: legs: pistol squat progressions, Bulgarian splits. Sat: skill practice, 20 min. Sun: rest.
